title.en: Volume 62 Biographies 50: Wang Pi, Wang Sizheng, Wei Chijiong, Wang Gui
title.raw: 卷六十二 列傳第五十: 王羆 王思政 尉遲迥 王軌 Volume 62 Biographies 50: Wang Pi, Wang Sizheng, Wei Chijiong, Wang Gui

sentences.zh: 王羆 王思政 尉遲迥 王軌

translations.literal: Wang Pi, Wang Sizheng, Wei Chijiong, Wang Gui
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi, Wang Sizheng, Wei Chijiong, and Wang Gui

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十

translations.literal: Biographies Fifty
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 50

sentences.zh: 王羆孫長述王思政尉遲迥弟綱綱子運王軌樂運

translations.literal: Wang Pi's grandson Changshu, Wang Sizheng, Wei Chijiong's younger brother Gang, Gang's son Yun, Wang Gui, Le Yun
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi (grandson Changshu), Wang Sizheng, Wei Chijiong (younger brother Gang; Gang's son Yun), Wang Gui, and Le Yun

sentences.zh: 王羆，字熊羆，京兆霸城人，漢河南尹遵之後，世為州郡著姓。

translations.literal: Wang Pi, courtesy name Xiongpi, was a native of Bache in Jingzhao. He was a descendant of Zun, Han Administrator of Henan, and his family for generations were eminent names in the provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi, whose courtesy name was Xiongpi, came from Bache in Jingzhao. He was descended from Zun, who had served as Administrator of Henan under the Han, and his clan had for generations been a prominent line in the provinces and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 羆質直木強，處物平當，州閭敬憚之。

translations.literal: Pi was upright by nature and stiffly honest; in dealing with affairs he was fair and even-handed, and the province and neighborhood both respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was blunt and uncompromising by nature, yet fair in his dealings; throughout the province people both respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 魏太和中，除殿中將軍，稍遷雍州別駕，清廉疾惡，勵精公事。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era of Wei he was appointed Palace Attendant General, and was gradually promoted to Vice Administrator of Yong Province. He was incorruptible and hated evil, and applied himself diligently to public business.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wei Taihe era he was appointed Palace Attendant General and was gradually promoted to Vice Administrator of Yong Province. Incorruptible and intolerant of wrongdoing, he threw himself into his official duties.

sentences.zh: 刺史崔亮有知人之鑒，見羆雅相欽挹。

translations.literal: The Inspector Cui Liang had a discerning eye for men, and on meeting Pi held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial inspector Cui Liang had a keen eye for talent, and when he met Pi he held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 亮後轉定州，啟羆為長史。

translations.literal: When Liang was later transferred to Ding Province, he recommended Pi as Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang was later transferred to Ding Province, he recommended Pi for the post of chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 執政者恐羆不稱，不許。

translations.literal: Those in power feared that Pi was not equal to the task and did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The men in power feared Pi was not up to the job and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 及梁人寇硤石，亮為都督南討，復啟羆為長史，帶銳軍。

translations.literal: When the Liang people raided Xiashi, Liang served as Commander for the southern campaign and again recommended Pi as Chief Administrator, with command of elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang forces raided Xiashi, Liang was made commander of the southern campaign and again recommended Pi as chief administrator, with command of elite troops.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以亮頻舉羆，故當可用。

translations.literal: The court, because Liang had repeatedly recommended Pi, concluded that he must be usable.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liang had repeatedly recommended Pi, the court concluded he must be fit for the role.

sentences.zh: 及克硤石，羆功居多。

translations.literal: When Xiashi was taken, Pi's merit was the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiashi was captured, Pi's contribution was the greatest of all.

sentences.zh: 先是南岐、東益氐羌反叛，乃拜羆冠軍將軍，鎮梁州，討平諸賊。

translations.literal: Earlier the Di and Qiang of South Qi and East Yi had rebelled, and Pi was appointed General Who Conquers the Enemy and stationed at Liang Province, where he suppressed and pacified the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Di and Qiang of South Qi and East Yi had risen in revolt, Pi was appointed General Who Conquers the Enemy and posted to Liang Province, where he put down the rebels.

sentences.zh: 還，授西河內史，辭不拜。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Administrator of Xihe, but he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was offered the post of Administrator of Xihe, but he declined it.

sentences.zh: 時人謂曰；

translations.literal: People of the time said to him:
translations.idiomatic: People at the time said to him:

sentences.zh: '西河大邦，奉祿優厚，何為致辭？

translations.literal: 'Xihe is a great commandery, and the salary is generous — why decline?'
translations.idiomatic: 'Xihe is a major commandery with a generous salary — why turn it down?'

sentences.zh: 」羆曰：「京洛材木，盡出西河，朝貴營第宅者，皆有求假。

translations.literal: Pi said: 'All the timber for the capital comes from Xihe, and every court noble building a mansion there asks to borrow it.'
translations.idiomatic: Pi replied, 'All the timber used in the capital comes from Xihe, and every court noble building a mansion there wants to borrow it.'

sentences.zh: 如其私辦，則力所不堪，若科發人間，又違犯憲法。

translations.literal: If I supply it from my own resources, my strength cannot bear it; if I levy it from the people, I violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: 'If I supply it from my own purse, I cannot afford it; if I levy it from the people, I break the law.'

sentences.zh: 以此致辭耳。」

translations.literal: That is why I decline.'
translations.idiomatic: That is why I am declining.'

sentences.zh: 後以軍功封定陽子，除荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Later, for military merit, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingyang and appointed Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his military achievements, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingyang and appointed inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 梁復遣曹義宗圍荊州，堰水灌城，不沒者數版。

translations.literal: Liang again sent Cao Yizong to besiege Jing Province, damming water to flood the city so that only a few courses of wall remained above water.
translations.idiomatic: Liang again sent Cao Yizong to besiege Jing Province, damming the waters to flood the city until only a few courses of wall stood above the water.

sentences.zh: 時既內外多虞，未遑救援，乃遺羆鐵券，雲城全當授本州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time there were many troubles at home and abroad, and no relief could be sent in time, so they sent Pi an iron certificate stating that if the city held he would be granted the original provincial post.
translations.idiomatic: With troubles at home and abroad, no relief could reach them in time, so the court sent Pi an iron certificate promising that if the city held, he would receive the provincial post in full.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，羆乃煮粥與將士均分食之。

translations.literal: When provisions in the city were exhausted, Pi cooked gruel and shared it equally with his officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When the city's grain ran out, Pi cooked gruel and shared it equally among his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 每出戰，常不擐甲胄，大呼告天曰：「荊州城，孝文皇帝所置。

translations.literal: Each time he went into battle he often wore no armor, and cried aloud to Heaven: 'Jing Province was established by Emperor Xiaowen.'
translations.idiomatic: Each time he went into battle he often wore no armor, crying aloud to Heaven, 'Jing Province was founded by Emperor Xiaowen.'

sentences.zh: 天若不佑國家，使箭中王羆額；

translations.literal: If Heaven does not protect the state, let an arrow strike Wang Pi in the forehead;
translations.idiomatic: 'If Heaven does not protect the state, let an arrow strike Wang Pi in the forehead;

sentences.zh: 不爾，王羆須破賊。

translations.literal: If not so, Wang Pi must destroy the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise Wang Pi must break the enemy.'

sentences.zh: 」屢經戰陣，亦不被傷。

translations.literal: He went through many battles and was never wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He fought through many battles and was never wounded.

sentences.zh: 彌曆三年，義宗方退。

translations.literal: After three full years Yizong finally withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After three full years, Yizong finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進封霸城縣公。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Duke of Bacheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Duke of Bacheng County.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，以羆為左軍大都督。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he appointed Pi Grand Commander of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he made Pi Grand Commander of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，莊帝以羆受顥官，故不得本州，更除岐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, Emperor Zhuang, because Pi had accepted office under Hao, would not grant him his original province and instead appointed him Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was defeated, Emperor Zhuang, because Pi had accepted office under him, denied him his original province and instead appointed him inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 時南秦數叛，以羆行南秦州事。

translations.literal: At the time South Qin rebelled repeatedly, and Pi was put in charge of South Qin Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time South Qin had rebelled repeatedly, and Pi was put in charge of South Qin Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 羆至州，召其魁帥為腹心，擊捕反者略盡。

translations.literal: When Pi reached the province, he summoned the chieftains to serve as his inner circle and hunted down the rebels until nearly all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi reached the province, he brought the chieftains close as trusted aides and hunted down the rebels until nearly all were captured.

sentences.zh: 乃謂魁帥等曰：「汝黨皆死盡，何用活為！

translations.literal: Then he said to the chieftains: 'Your followers are all dead — what use is living!'
translations.idiomatic: Then he told the chieftains, 'Your followers are all dead — what point is there in living?'

sentences.zh: 」乃以次斬之。

translations.literal: Then in order he beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Then he had them beheaded one by one.

sentences.zh: 自是南秦無復反者。

translations.literal: From then on there were no more rebels in South Qin.
translations.idiomatic: After that there were no more rebellions in South Qin.

sentences.zh: 又詔羆行秦州事。

translations.literal: Again he ordered Pi to administer Qin Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to administer Qin Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋遷涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 未及之部，屬周文帝徵兵為勤王之舉，羆請前驅效命，遂為大都督，鎮華州。

translations.literal: Before he could reach his post, Duke Wen of Zhou was raising troops to rescue the throne, and Pi asked to serve in the vanguard. He was made Grand Commander and stationed at Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his post, Duke Wen of Zhou was raising troops to rescue the throne. Pi volunteered to lead the vanguard and was made grand commander, stationed at Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司，別封萬年縣伯，乃除華州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Pi was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and given the third rank of honorary equivalence, separately enfeoffed as Baron of Wannian County, and appointed Inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Pi was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with third-rank honorary equivalence, separately enfeoffed as Baron of Wannian County, and appointed inspector of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 齊神武率軍進潼關，人懷危懼，羆勸勱交士，眾心乃安。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan of Qi led his army to Tong Pass, people were filled with fear, but Pi encouraged and rallied the gentry and soldiers, and the people's hearts were settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan of Qi led his army to Tong Pass, fear spread among the people, but Pi rallied the gentry and soldiers until morale steadied.

sentences.zh: 神武退，拜驃騎大將軍，加侍中、開府。

translations.literal: Gao Huan withdrew; [Pi] was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, with added titles Palace Attendant and Opener of the Mansion.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan withdrew, Pi was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, with the additional titles of Palace Attendant and Opener of the Mansion.

sentences.zh: 嘗修州城未畢，梯在城外。

translations.literal: Once, while repairs to the provincial city wall were not yet finished, the ladders were left outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while repairs to the provincial city wall were still unfinished, the ladders were left outside the wall.

sentences.zh: 神武遣韓軌、司馬子如從河東宵濟襲羆，羆不覺。

translations.literal: Gao Huan sent Han Gui and Sima Ziru to cross from Hedong by night and raid Pi; Pi did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent Han Gui and Sima Ziru to cross the river at night from Hedong and raid Pi, and Pi did not notice.

sentences.zh: 比曉，軌眾已乘梯入城。

translations.literal: By dawn, Gui's troops had already mounted ladders and entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn, Gui's troops had already climbed the ladders into the city.

sentences.zh: 羆尚臥未起，聞閣外洶洶有聲，便袒身露髻徒跣，持一白棒，大呼而出，謂曰：「老羆當道臥，貉子那得過！

translations.literal: Pi was still asleep and had not risen when he heard a clamor outside the gate. He bared his torso, let down his hair, went barefoot, took a white club, and rushed out shouting: 'Old Pi lies across the road — how can you foxes get past!'
translations.idiomatic: Pi was still asleep when he heard a clamor outside the gate. He bared his torso, let down his hair, went barefoot, seized a white club, and rushed out shouting, 'Old Pi lies across the road — how can you foxes get past!'

sentences.zh: 」敵見，驚退。

translations.literal: The enemy saw him and retreated in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy saw him and fell back in alarm.

sentences.zh: 逐至東門，左右稍集，合戰破之。

translations.literal: He pursued them to the east gate; his attendants gradually gathered, and together they fought and routed the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them to the east gate; as his men gradually gathered, they joined battle and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 軌遂投城遁走。

translations.literal: Gui then cast himself from the wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gui then leapt from the wall and fled.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞而壯之。

translations.literal: Duke Wen heard and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Wen heard of it, he admired Pi's courage.

sentences.zh: 時關中大饑，徵稅人間穀食，以供軍費。

translations.literal: At the time Guanzhong suffered great famine, and grain was levied from the people to supply military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Guanzhong was in famine, and grain was levied from the people to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 或隱匿者，令遞相告，多被篣捶，以是人有逃散。

translations.literal: Those who concealed grain were made to inform on one another, and many were beaten with rods, so people fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hid grain were made to inform on one another, and many were beaten with rods, so people fled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 唯羆信著于人，莫有隱者，得粟不少諸州，而無怨讟。

translations.literal: Only Pi's trustworthiness was well established among the people; no one concealed grain, and the grain collected was no less than in other provinces, yet there was no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Pi, whose trustworthiness was well established, did no one conceal grain. He collected no less than other provinces, yet without complaint.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之役，神武士馬甚盛。

translations.literal: At the battle of Shahu, Gao Huan's soldiers and horses were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Shahu, Gao Huan's troops and horses were very strong.

sentences.zh: 文帝以華州沖要，遣使勞羆，令加守備。

translations.literal: Duke Wen, because Hua Province was strategically vital, sent an envoy to encourage Pi and ordered him to strengthen the defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hua Province was strategically vital, Duke Wen sent an envoy to encourage Pi and ordered him to strengthen the defenses.

sentences.zh: 及神武至城下，謂羆曰；

translations.literal: When Gao Huan reached the foot of the city wall, he said to Pi:
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan reached the foot of the wall, he said to Pi:

sentences.zh: 「何不早降？

translations.literal: 'Why not surrender early?'
translations.idiomatic: 'Why not surrender now?'

sentences.zh: 」羆乃大呼曰：「此城是王羆家，死生在此，欲死者來！

translations.literal: Pi then shouted loudly: 'This city is Wang Pi's home; life and death are here — let those who wish to die come!'
translations.idiomatic: Pi shouted back, 'This city is Wang Pi's home. Life and death are here — let those who wish to die come!'

sentences.zh: 」神武不敢攻。

translations.literal: Gao Huan did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 後移鎮河東，以前後功進爵扶風郡公。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to command Hedong, and for his cumulative merits was advanced to Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to command Hedong, and for his cumulative service was promoted to Duke of Fufeng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 河橋之戰，王師不利，趙青雀據長安城，所在莫有固志。

translations.literal: At the battle of Heqiao the royal army fared badly, Zhao Qingque seized Chang'an, and everywhere men lacked firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Heqiao the royal army was defeated, Zhao Qingque seized Chang'an, and resolve collapsed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 羆乃大開州門，召城中戰士謂曰：「如聞天子敗績，不知吉凶，諸人相驚，咸有異望。

translations.literal: Pi then threw open the provincial gates, summoned the warriors in the city, and said: 'I hear the Son of Heaven has been defeated and do not know whether he lives or dies. You are all alarmed and harbor other designs.'
translations.idiomatic: Pi threw open the provincial gates, summoned the warriors in the city, and said, 'I hear the emperor has been defeated and do not know his fate. You are all alarmed and harbor other designs.'

sentences.zh: 王羆受委於此，以死報恩。

translations.literal: Wang Pi has been entrusted here and will repay that trust with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi has been entrusted with this post and will repay that trust with his life.

sentences.zh: 諸人若有異圖，可來見殺。

translations.literal: If any of you have other designs, you may come and kill me.
translations.idiomatic: If any of you have other designs, come and kill me.

sentences.zh: 必恐城陷沒者，亦任出城。

translations.literal: Those who fear the city will sink and perish may also leave the city as they wish.
translations.idiomatic: If you fear the city will fall, you are free to leave.

sentences.zh: 如有忠誠，能與王羆同心，可共固守。

translations.literal: If you are loyal and can share Wang Pi's resolve, we may hold the city together.
translations.idiomatic: If you are loyal and share Wang Pi's resolve, we can hold the city together.

sentences.zh: 」軍人見其誠信，皆無異心。

translations.literal: The soldiers, seeing his sincerity and trustworthiness, all abandoned other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his sincerity, the soldiers all abandoned other designs.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，徵拜雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was summoned and appointed Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was summoned and appointed inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 是蠕蠕度河南寇，候騎已至豳州。

translations.literal: At that time the Rouran crossed the Yellow River southward to raid, and their scouts had already reached Bin Province.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Rouran crossed the Yellow River to raid, and their scouts had already reached Bin Province.

sentences.zh: 朝廷慮其深入，乃徵發士馬，屯守京城，塹諸街巷，以備侵軼。

translations.literal: The court, fearing a deep incursion, mobilized troops and horses, garrisoned the capital, and dug trenches in the streets to guard against raids.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a deep incursion, the court mobilized troops, garrisoned the capital, and dug trenches in the streets against raids.

sentences.zh: 右僕射周惠達召羆議之。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Zhou Huida summoned Pi to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Vice Director Zhou Huida summoned Pi to discuss the matter.

sentences.zh: 羆不應命，臥而不起，謂其使曰：「若蠕蠕至渭北者，王羆率鄉里自破之，不煩國家兵。

translations.literal: Pi did not respond to the summons, but lay abed and would not rise, telling the messenger: 'If the Rouran reach the north bank of the Wei, Wang Pi will lead the local people to defeat them himself, without troubling the state's troops.'
translations.idiomatic: Pi did not respond but lay abed, telling the messenger, 'If the Rouran reach the north bank of the Wei, Wang Pi will lead the local people to defeat them without troubling the state's troops.'

sentences.zh: 何為天子城中，遂作如此驚動！

translations.literal: Why cause such alarm in the Son of Heaven's city!'
translations.idiomatic: Why cause such panic in the emperor's city!'

sentences.zh: 由周家小兒恇怯致此。

translations.literal: This is caused by the cowardice of that Zhou boy.'
translations.idiomatic: This is the cowardice of that Zhou boy.'

sentences.zh: 」羆輕侮權貴，守正不回，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Pi's light contempt for the powerful and steadfast integrity without deviation were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's contempt for the powerful and his steadfast integrity were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 未幾，還鎮河東。

translations.literal: Before long, he returned to garrison Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to command Hedong.

sentences.zh: 羆性儉率，不事邊幅。

translations.literal: Pi was frugal and plain by nature and did not trouble himself with appearances.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was frugal and plain by nature and cared nothing for appearances.

sentences.zh: 嘗有台使至，羆為設食，使乃裂去薄餅緣。

translations.literal: Once when a court envoy arrived, Pi set out food for him, and the envoy tore off the edges of the thin cakes.
translations.idiomatic: Once when a court envoy arrived, Pi set out food, and the envoy tore off the edges of the thin cakes.

sentences.zh: 羆曰：「耕種收穫，其功已深，舂爨造成，用力不少，爾之選擇，當是未饑。

translations.literal: Pi said: 'To plant and harvest requires deep labor; to pound grain and cook it takes no small effort. Your picking and choosing shows you cannot be hungry.'
translations.idiomatic: Pi said, 'Planting and harvesting take deep labor; pounding grain and cooking it take no small effort. Your picking and choosing shows you cannot be hungry.'

sentences.zh: 」命左右撤去之。

translations.literal: He ordered attendants to remove it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to take the food away.

sentences.zh: 使者愕然大慚。

translations.literal: The envoy was stunned and greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was stunned and deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 又客與羆食瓜，客削瓜皮，侵肉稍厚，羆意嫌之。

translations.literal: Again, when a guest was eating melon with Pi, the guest peeled the rind and cut away rather too much flesh, which Pi resented.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when a guest was eating melon with Pi, the guest peeled away rather too much flesh along with the rind, which Pi resented.

sentences.zh: 及瓜皮落地，乃引手就地取而食之。

translations.literal: When the melon rind fell to the ground, he reached hand to the ground, took it, and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rind fell to the ground, he reached down, picked it up, and ate it.

sentences.zh: 客甚愧色。

translations.literal: The guest had a very ashamed expression.
translations.idiomatic: The guest was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 性又嚴急，嘗有吏挾私陳事者，羆不暇命捶撲，乃手自取鞾履，持以擊之。

translations.literal: His nature was also stern and quick-tempered. Once when an official came with a private petition, Pi had no time to order a beating and took up his boots himself to strike the man.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was also stern and quick-tempered. Once when an official came with a private petition, Pi had no time to order a beating and seized his boots to strike the man himself.

sentences.zh: 每至享會，自秤量酒肉，分給將士。

translations.literal: At every feast he personally weighed out wine and meat and distributed it to the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At every feast he personally weighed out wine and meat and distributed it to his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 時人尚其均平，嗤其鄙碎。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his fairness but mocked his petty fussiness.
translations.idiomatic: People admired his fairness but mocked his petty fussiness.

sentences.zh: 羆舉動率情，不為巧詐，凡所經處，雖無當時功跡，咸去乃見思。

translations.literal: Pi acted according to his feelings and practiced no cunning deceit. Wherever he served, though he left no conspicuous achievements at the time, after he departed he was missed.
translations.idiomatic: Pi acted from the heart and practiced no cunning. Wherever he served, though he left no conspicuous achievements at the time, he was missed after he departed.

sentences.zh: 卒于官，贈太尉、都督、相冀等十州刺史，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Commandant and Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of ten provinces including Xiang and Ji; his posthumous name was Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Commandant, Commander-in-Chief, and Inspector of ten provinces including Xiang and Ji; his posthumous name was Loyal.

sentences.zh: 羆安於貧素，不營生業，後雖貴顯，鄉里舊宅，不改衡門，身死之日，家甚貧罄，當時伏其清潔。

translations.literal: Pi was content with poverty and simplicity and did not pursue a livelihood. Though later he rose to high rank, he did not alter the simple gate of his old home in the countryside, and on the day he died his household was very poor and empty; people of the time admired his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was content with poverty and simplicity and did not pursue wealth. Though he later rose to high rank, he left the simple gate of his old country home unchanged, and when he died his household was very poor; people of the time admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 子慶遠，弱冠以功臣子拜直閣將軍，先羆卒。

translations.literal: His son Qingyuan, upon reaching adulthood as the son of a meritorious official, was appointed Direct Attendant General, and died before Pi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qingyuan, upon reaching adulthood as the son of a meritorious official, was appointed Direct Attendant General and died before Pi.

sentences.zh: 孫述。

translations.literal: His grandson Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Shu.

sentences.zh: 子謨嗣。

translations.literal: His son Mo succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 謨弟軌，大業末郡守。

translations.literal: Mo's younger brother Gui was a commandery administrator at the end of the Daye era.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's younger brother Gui was a commandery administrator at the end of the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 少子文楷，起部郎。

translations.literal: The youngest son Wenkai was a Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son Wenkai was a Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 王思政，太原祁人，漢司徒允之後也。

translations.literal: Wang Sizheng was a native of Qi in Taiyuan and a descendant of Wang Yun, Han Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng came from Qi in Taiyuan and was a descendant of Wang Yun, Minister over the Masses under the Han.

sentences.zh: 自魏太尉淩誅後，冠冕遂絕。

translations.literal: From after the Wei Grand Commandant Ling was executed, official caps and robes ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei Grand Commandant Ling was executed, the family's official standing came to an end.

sentences.zh: 父佑，州主簿。

translations.literal: His father You was a provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His father You was a provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 思政容貌魁梧，有籌策，解褐員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Sizheng was tall and imposing in appearance, possessed of strategic talent, and upon leaving the commoner's robe was appointed Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng was tall and imposing, possessed of strategic talent, and upon entering office was appointed Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 屬万俟醜奴、宿勤明達等擾亂關右，北海王顥討之，聞思政壯健，啟與隨軍，所有謀議，並與參詳。

translations.literal: When Moqi Chounu, Suqin Mingda, and others were disturbing the lands west of the Pass, Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao went to suppress them. Hearing that Sizheng was strong and capable, he recommended him to accompany the army, and in all planning and deliberation Sizheng took part.
translations.idiomatic: When Moqi Chounu, Suqin Mingda, and others were raiding the lands west of the Pass, Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao marched against them. Hearing that Sizheng was strong and capable, he had him join the campaign, and Sizheng took part in all planning and deliberation.

sentences.zh: 時孝武在籓，素聞其名，乃引為賓客，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xiaowu was still a prince and had long heard Sizheng's name, so he took him on as a guest and treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Xiaowu was still a prince and had long heard of Sizheng, so he took him on as a retainer and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 及登大位，委以心膂。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he entrusted Sizheng as a pillar of his rule.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne, he entrusted Sizheng as one of his closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 預定策功，封祁縣侯，為武衛將軍。

translations.literal: For merit in settling the succession he was enfeoffed Marquis of Qi County and made General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in settling the succession he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qi County and appointed General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 俄而齊神武潛有異圖，帝以思政可任大事，拜使持節、中軍大將軍、大都督，總宿衛兵。

translations.literal: Soon Gao Huan of Qi secretly had other designs; the emperor, deeming Sizheng capable of great affairs, appointed him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of the Central Army, Grand Commander, with overall command of palace guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gao Huan of Qi secretly harbored other designs, and the emperor, believing Sizheng capable of great affairs, appointed him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of the Central Army, and Grand Commander, with overall command of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 思政乃言於帝曰：「洛陽四面受敵，非用武之地。

translations.literal: Sizheng then said to the emperor: 'Luoyang is beset on all sides and is no place for making war.'
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng then told the emperor, 'Luoyang is beset on all sides and is no place to make war.'

sentences.zh: 關中有崤函之固，且士馬精強。

translations.literal: Guanzhong has the stronghold of Xiao and Han, and moreover soldiers and horses are elite and strong.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong has the strongholds of Xiao and Han, and its troops and horses are elite and powerful.

sentences.zh: 宇文夏州糾合同盟，願立功效若聞車駕西幸，必當奔走奉迎。

translations.literal: Commandant Yuwen of Xia Province has rallied the allied forces and wishes to prove his worth; if he hears the imperial carriage is moving west, he will surely rush to welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Yuwen of Xia Province has rallied the allied forces and wishes to prove his worth. If he hears the imperial carriage is moving west, he will surely rush to welcome it.

sentences.zh: 藉天府之資，因已成之業，二年修復舊京，何慮不克。

translations.literal: Relying on the resources of the imperial domain and building on work already accomplished, in two years the old capital can be restored — why fear failure?
translations.idiomatic: With the resources of the imperial domain and work already accomplished, the old capital can be restored in two years — why fear failure?

sentences.zh: 」帝深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply agreed.

sentences.zh: 及神武兵至河北，帝乃西遷。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan's army reached Hebei, the emperor then moved west.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan's army reached Hebei, the emperor moved west.

sentences.zh: 進爵太原郡公，拜光祿卿、并州刺史，加散騎常侍、大都督。

translations.literal: Sizheng was advanced to Duke of Taiyuan Commandery, appointed Minister of the Imperial Household and Inspector of Bing Province, and given the additional titles of Regular Attendant Cavalier and Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng was promoted to Duke of Taiyuan Commandery, appointed Minister of the Imperial Household and inspector of Bing Province, and given the additional titles of Regular Attendant Cavalier and Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 大統之後，思政雖被任委，自以非相府之舊，每不自安。

translations.literal: After the Dazong era, though Sizheng was entrusted with duties, he considered himself not an old associate of the chancellor's house and was often ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dazong era, though Sizheng was entrusted with office, he felt himself not an old associate of the chancellor's house and was often ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 周文帝曾在同州，與群公宴集，出錦罽及雜綾絹數千段，令諸將摴蒲取之。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Zhou was once at Tong Province, feasting with the nobles; he brought out several thousand bolts of brocade and assorted silks and had the generals play pitch-pot to take them.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Zhou was once at Tong Province and held a banquet with the nobles. He brought out several thousand bolts of brocade and assorted silks and had the generals play pitch-pot to win them.

sentences.zh: 物盡，周文又解所服金帶，令諸人遍擲，曰：「先得盧者即與之。

translations.literal: When the goods were exhausted, Duke Wen again removed the gold belt he was wearing and had everyone take turns casting lots, saying: 'Whoever first gets the winning throw shall have it.'
translations.idiomatic: When the goods were exhausted, Duke Wen removed the gold belt he was wearing and had everyone take turns casting lots, saying, 'Whoever first gets the winning throw shall have it.'

sentences.zh: 」群公擲將遍，莫有得者。

translations.literal: The nobles cast until all were done; none obtained [a prize].
translations.idiomatic: The nobles cast until all had had their turn, but none won.

sentences.zh: 次至思政，乃斂容跪而誓曰：「王思政羈旅歸朝，蒙宰相國士之遇，方願盡心效命，上報知已。

translations.literal: When it came to Sizheng's turn, he composed his expression, knelt, and swore: 'Wang Sizheng, a wanderer who returned to the court, has received from the chancellor the treatment due a national champion and now wishes to devote himself and repay that trust.'
translations.idiomatic: When it came to Sizheng's turn, he composed his expression, knelt, and swore, 'Wang Sizheng, a wanderer who returned to the court, has received from the chancellor the treatment due a national champion and now wishes to devote himself and repay that trust.'

sentences.zh: 若此誠有實，令宰相賜知者，願擲即為盧；

translations.literal: If this sincerity truly exists and Heaven lets the chancellor know, may my cast immediately be the winning throw;
translations.idiomatic: If this sincerity is true and Heaven lets the chancellor know it, may my cast be the winning throw;

sentences.zh: 若內懷不盡，神靈亦當明之，使不作也，便當殺身以謝所奉。

translations.literal: if my inner heart is not complete, the spirits also ought to make it clear, causing it not to succeed; then I should kill myself to answer what I have pledged.
translations.idiomatic: if my heart is not wholly loyal, the spirits will make it clear and my cast will fail, and I shall kill myself to answer for what I have pledged.'

sentences.zh: 」辭氣慷慨，一座盡驚。

translations.literal: His words and spirit were impassioned; the whole assembly was astonished.
translations.idiomatic: His words were impassioned, and the whole assembly was astonished.

sentences.zh: 即拔所佩刀，橫於膝上，攬摴蒲，拊髀擲之。

translations.literal: At once he drew the sword at his belt, laid it across his knees, gathered the pitch-pot pieces, slapped his thigh, and cast.
translations.idiomatic: He at once drew the sword at his belt, laid it across his knees, gathered the pitch-pot pieces, slapped his thigh, and cast.

sentences.zh: 比周文止之，已擲為盧矣。

translations.literal: By the time Duke Wen stopped him, he had already cast the winning throw.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Duke Wen stopped him, he had already cast the winning throw.

sentences.zh: 徐乃拜而受帶。

translations.literal: Then slowly he bowed and received the belt.
translations.idiomatic: Then he bowed and received the belt.

sentences.zh: 自此朝寄更深。

translations.literal: From this the court's trust in him grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the court's trust in him grew deeper.

sentences.zh: 及河橋之戰，思政下馬，用長槊左右橫擊，一擊踣數人。

translations.literal: At the battle of Heqiao, Sizheng dismounted, used a long spear to strike left and right horizontally; one strike felled several men.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Heqiao, Sizheng dismounted, took a long spear, and struck left and right; with each blow he felled several men.

sentences.zh: 時陷陣既深，從者死盡，思政被重創悶絕。

translations.literal: At that time having penetrated the formation deeply, his followers were all dead; Sizheng suffered heavy wounds and lost consciousness.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had penetrated deep into the enemy formation, his followers were all dead, and Sizheng suffered grave wounds and lost consciousness.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，敵亦收軍。

translations.literal: As it happened dusk fell; the enemy also withdrew troops.
translations.idiomatic: As dusk fell, the enemy also withdrew.

sentences.zh: 思政久經軍旅，戰唯著破衣弊甲，敵人疑非將帥，故得免。

translations.literal: Sizheng had long been in the army; in battle he wore only tattered clothes and worn armor; the enemy doubted he was not a commander, and thus he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng had long served in the army and in battle wore only tattered clothes and worn armor, so the enemy doubted he was a commander and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 有帳下督雷五安于戰處哭求思政，會已蘇，遂相得。

translations.literal: There was a camp adjutant Lei Wu'an who wept and sought Sizheng on the battlefield; Sizheng had already revived, and they found each other.
translations.idiomatic: A camp adjutant named Lei Wu'an wept and searched for Sizheng on the battlefield; Sizheng had already revived, and they found each other.

sentences.zh: 乃割衣裹創，扶思政上馬，夜久方得還軍。

translations.literal: Then they cut cloth to wrap his wounds, helped Sizheng mount a horse; only after a long night did they return to the army.
translations.idiomatic: They tore cloth to bind his wounds, helped Sizheng mount a horse, and only late at night reached their army.

sentences.zh: 仍鎮弘農，除侍中、東道行台。

translations.literal: He still garrisoned Hongnong; was appointed Palace Attendant and Eastern Route Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to command Hongnong and was appointed Palace Attendant and Eastern Route Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 思政以玉壁地險要，請築城。

translations.literal: Sizheng, because Yubi was strategically vital, requested that a fortress be built there.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yubi was strategically vital, Sizheng requested that a fortress be built there.

sentences.zh: 即自營度，移鎮之。

translations.literal: At once he personally planned and measured, and moved his garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: He personally planned the work and moved his command there.

sentences.zh: 管汾晉並三州諸軍事、并州刺史、行台如故，仍鎮玉壁。

translations.literal: He continued to administer military affairs of the three provinces of Fen, Jin, and Bing, to serve as Inspector of Bing Province and Commissioner as before, and remained stationed at Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to administer military affairs of the three provinces of Fen, Jin, and Bing, to serve as inspector of Bing Province and commissioner as before, and remained stationed at Yubi.

sentences.zh: 八年，東魏復來寇，卒不能克。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Eastern Wei again came to raid; in the end could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Eastern Wei again came to raid, but in the end could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 以全城功，授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: For the merit of holding the city intact, he was granted General of Agile Cavalry and Opener of the Mansion with third-rank honorary equivalence.
translations.idiomatic: For holding the city intact, he was granted General of Agile Cavalry and Opener of the Mansion with third-rank honorary equivalence.

sentences.zh: 高仲密以北豫州來附，周文親接援之，乃驛召思政，將鎮成皋。

translations.literal: Gao Zhongmi came over with North Yuzhou, and Duke Wen personally went to receive and support him, then summoned Sizheng by express post to command Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi came over with North Yuzhou, Duke Wen personally went to receive and support him, then summoned Sizheng by express post to command Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 未至而班師，復命思政鎮弘農。

translations.literal: Before arriving the army withdrew; again he was ordered to garrison Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived the army withdrew, and he was again ordered to command Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 思政入弘農，令開城門，解衣而臥，慰勉將士，示不足畏。

translations.literal: Sizheng entered Hongnong, ordered the city gates opened, removed his outer robe and lay down, encouraging the officers and soldiers and showing that there was nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng entered Hongnong, ordered the city gates opened, removed his outer robe and lay down, encouraging his officers and men and showing there was nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 數日後，東魏將劉豐生率數千騎至城下，憚之，不敢進，乃引軍還。

translations.literal: Several days later the Eastern Wei general Liu Fengsheng led several thousand horsemen to the foot of the wall, feared this display, dared not advance, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the Eastern Wei general Liu Fengsheng led several thousand horsemen to the foot of the wall, was intimidated by this display, dared not advance, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是修城郭，起樓櫓，營田農，積芻秣，凡可以守禦者皆具焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired walls and moats, raised towers and parapets, opened fields for farming, stored fodder and grain; all that could be used for defense was provided.
translations.idiomatic: Then he repaired the walls and moats, built towers and parapets, opened fields, stored fodder and grain, and provided everything needed for defense.

sentences.zh: 弘農之有備，自思政始也。

translations.literal: Hongnong's preparedness began from Sizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hongnong's preparedness began with Sizheng.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加特進，兼尚書左僕射、行台、都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was given the special advance rank and concurrently appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Commissioner, Commander-in-Chief, and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was given the special advance rank and concurrently appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, commissioner, commander-in-chief, and inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 境內卑濕，城塹多壞。

translations.literal: Within the territory it was low and damp; walls and moats were largely ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The territory was low and damp, and the walls and moats were largely ruined.

sentences.zh: 思政乃命都督藺小歡督工匠繕修之。

translations.literal: Sizheng then ordered the Commander Lin Xiaohuan to supervise craftsmen in repairing them.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng then ordered Commander Lin Xiaohuan to supervise craftsmen in repairing them.

sentences.zh: 掘得黃金三十斤，夜中密送。

translations.literal: Thirty jin of gold were dug up and secretly sent at night.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty jin of gold were unearthed and secretly sent to him at night.

sentences.zh: 至旦，思政召佐史，以金示之曰：「人臣不宜有私。

translations.literal: At dawn Sizheng summoned his clerks, showed them the gold, and said: 'A subject should not keep private property.'
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Sizheng summoned his clerks, showed them the gold, and said, 'A subject should not keep private property.'

sentences.zh: 」悉封金送上。

translations.literal: He sealed all the gold and sent it up.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed all the gold and sent it up to the court.

sentences.zh: 周文嘉之，賜錢二十萬。

translations.literal: Duke Wen praised this and granted two hundred thousand coins.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen praised this and granted him two hundred thousand coins.

sentences.zh: 思政之去玉壁也，周文命舉代人，思政乃進所部都督韋孝寬。

translations.literal: When Sizheng was leaving Yubi, Duke Wen ordered that a replacement be recommended; Sizheng then advanced his subordinate Commander Wei Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Sizheng was leaving Yubi, Duke Wen ordered that a replacement be recommended, and Sizheng advanced his subordinate Commander Wei Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 其後東魏來寇，孝寬卒能全城，時論稱其知人。

translations.literal: Later when Eastern Wei came to raid, Xiaokuan was able to hold the city intact, and opinion at the time praised Sizheng's judgment of men.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Eastern Wei came to raid, Xiaokuan held the city intact, and opinion at the time praised Sizheng's judgment of men.

sentences.zh: 十三年，侯景叛東魏，請援乞師。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Hou Jing rebelled against Eastern Wei and requested aid and troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Hou Jing rebelled against Eastern Wei and asked for aid and troops.

sentences.zh: 當時未即應接。

translations.literal: At the time there was no immediate response.
translations.idiomatic: At the time no immediate response was made.

sentences.zh: 思政以為若不因機進取，後悔無及，即率荊州步騎萬餘，從魯關向陽翟。

translations.literal: Sizheng thought that if they did not seize the opportunity to advance and take, regret would have no end; at once he led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry from Jing Province from Lu Pass toward Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng believed that if they did not seize the opportunity, regret would come too late, and immediately led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry from Jing Province from Lu Pass toward Yangdi.

sentences.zh: 周文聞思政已發，乃遣太尉李弼赴潁川。

translations.literal: When Duke Wen heard Sizheng had already set out, he sent Grand Commandant Li Bi to Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Wen heard that Sizheng had already set out, he sent Grand Commandant Li Bi to Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 東魏將高岳等聞大軍至，收軍而遁。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei generals Gao Yue and others, hearing the great army had arrived, gathered troops and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei generals Gao Yue and others, hearing that the main army had arrived, withdrew and fled.

sentences.zh: 思政入守潁川。

translations.literal: Sizheng entered and defended Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng entered and defended Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 景引兵向豫州，外稱略地，乃密遣送款于梁。

translations.literal: Jing led troops toward Yuzhou, outwardly claiming to seize territory, but secretly sent submission to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Jing led his troops toward Yuzhou, outwardly claiming to seize territory, but secretly sent submission to Liang.

sentences.zh: 先是，周文遣帥都督賀蘭願德助景扞禦，景既有異圖，因厚撫願德等，冀為己用。

translations.literal: Earlier Duke Wen had sent Commander-in-Chief Helan Yuande to help Jing in defense; once Jing had other designs, he treated Yuande and others generously, hoping to win them for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Duke Wen had sent Commander-in-Chief Helan Yuande to help Jing in defense. Once Jing had other designs, he treated Yuande and the others generously, hoping to win them to his side.

sentences.zh: 思政知景詭詐，乃密追願德。

translations.literal: Sizheng knew Jing's deceit and secretly recalled Yuande.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng knew Jing's deceit and secretly recalled Yuande.

sentences.zh: 思政分佈諸軍，據景七州十二鎮。

translations.literal: Sizheng deployed the armies and occupied Jing's seven provinces and twelve garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng deployed his forces and seized Jing's seven provinces and twelve garrisons.

sentences.zh: 周文乃以所授景使持節、太傅、大將軍，兼尚書令、河南大行台、河南諸軍事，回授思政，思政並讓不受。

translations.literal: Duke Wen then transferred to Sizheng the titles granted to Jing — Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Tutor, Grand General, concurrent Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Commissioner of Henan, Commander of Henan Military Affairs — but Sizheng declined all.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen then transferred to Sizheng the titles granted to Jing — Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Tutor, Grand General, concurrent Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Commissioner of Henan, and Commander of Henan Military Affairs — but Sizheng declined them all.

sentences.zh: 頻使敦喻，唯受河南諸軍事。

translations.literal: Messengers repeatedly urged him; he accepted only command of Henan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Messengers repeatedly urged him, and he accepted only command of Henan military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十四年，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 九月，東魏太尉高岳、行台慕容紹宗、儀同劉豐生等率步騎十萬來攻潁川，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Eastern Wei Grand Commandant Gao Yue, Commissioner Murong Shaozong, Liu Fengsheng with honorary third rank, and others led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Yingchuan, killing and wounding very many.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Eastern Wei Grand Commandant Gao Yue, Commissioner Murong Shaozong, Liu Fengsheng with honorary third rank, and others led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Yingchuan, inflicting heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 岳又築土山以臨城中，飛梯火車，盡攻擊之法。

translations.literal: Yue also built earthen mounds overlooking the city, flying ladders and fire carts — every method of attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yue also built earthen mounds overlooking the city and used flying ladders and fire carts — every method of assault.

sentences.zh: 思政亦作火<矛贊>，因迅風便投之土山。

translations.literal: Sizheng also made fire projectiles and, taking advantage of a swift wind, hurled them at the earthen mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng also made fire projectiles and, taking advantage of a swift wind, hurled them at the earthen mounds.

sentences.zh: 又射以火箭，燒其攻具。

translations.literal: He also shot fire arrows and burned their siege equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He also shot fire arrows and burned their siege equipment.

sentences.zh: 仍募勇士，縋而出戰，據其兩土山，置樓堞以助防守。

translations.literal: He also recruited brave men, lowered them by rope to sally forth, seized two earthen mounds, and built parapets to aid defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited brave men, lowered them by rope to sally forth, seized two of the earthen mounds, and built parapets on them to aid the defense.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄更益兵，堰洧水以灌城。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng of Qi sent more troops and dammed the Wei River to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng of Qi sent more troops and dammed the Wei River to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 時雖有怪獸，每沖壞其堰。

translations.literal: At the time there were strange beasts that repeatedly broke the dam.
translations.idiomatic: At the time strange beasts repeatedly broke the dam.

sentences.zh: 然城被灌已久，多亦崩頹。

translations.literal: Yet the city had been flooded long; much also collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the city had been flooded for a long time, and much of the wall had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 嶽悉眾苦攻。

translations.literal: Yue mustered all forces and pressed the attack bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Yue mustered all his forces and pressed the attack bitterly.

sentences.zh: 思政身當矢石，與士卒同勞苦。

translations.literal: Sizheng personally faced arrows and stones and shared labor and hardship with the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng placed himself in the path of arrows and stones and shared hardship with his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 岳乃更修堰，作鐵龍雜獸，用厭水神。

translations.literal: Yue then rebuilt the dam and made iron dragons and assorted beasts to subdue the water spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then rebuilt the dam and made iron dragons and assorted beasts to subdue the water spirit.

sentences.zh: 堰成，水大至。

translations.literal: When the dam was finished, the water rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When the dam was finished, the water rose greatly.

sentences.zh: 城中泉湧溢，懸釜而炊，糧力俱竭。

translations.literal: Springs gushed within the city; pots were hung to cook; grain and strength were both exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Springs gushed within the city, pots had to be hung to cook, and both grain and strength were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 慕容紹宗、劉豐生及其將慕容永珍意以為閑，共乘樓船以望城內，令善射人俯射城中。

translations.literal: Murong Shaozong, Liu Fengsheng, and their general Murong Yongzhen, thinking the situation leisurely, together boarded a tower ship to look into the city and ordered skilled archers to shoot down into it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shaozong, Liu Fengsheng, and their general Murong Yongzhen, thinking the situation secure, together boarded a tower ship to look into the city and ordered skilled archers to shoot down into it.

sentences.zh: 俄而大風暴起，船乃飄至城下。

translations.literal: Soon a great wind arose; the ship drifted to the foot of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a great wind arose, and the ship drifted to the foot of the wall.

sentences.zh: 城上人以長鉤牽船，弓弩亂髮。

translations.literal: Men on the wall used long hooks to pull the ship; bows and crossbows were loosed in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the wall used long hooks to pull the ship and shot bows and crossbows in a wild volley.

sentences.zh: 紹宗竊急，透水而死。

translations.literal: Shaozong, in secret panic, drowned while crossing the water.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong, in panic, drowned while crossing the water.

sentences.zh: 豐生浮向土山，復中矢而斃。

translations.literal: Fengsheng floated toward an earthen mound and was again struck by an arrow and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fengsheng floated toward an earthen mound and was struck by an arrow and killed.

sentences.zh: 禽永珍，並獲船中器械。

translations.literal: Yongzhen was captured; equipment on the ship was also obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhen was captured, and the equipment on the ship was also taken.

sentences.zh: 思政謂永珍曰：「僕之破亡，在於晷漏。

translations.literal: Sizheng said to Yongzhen: 'My ruin is only a matter of hours.'
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng said to Yongzhen, 'My ruin is only a matter of hours.'

sentences.zh: 誠知殺卿無益，然人臣之節，守之以死。

translations.literal: I truly know that killing you would serve no purpose, yet a subject's duty must be kept unto death.'
translations.idiomatic: I know killing you would serve no purpose, yet a subject's duty must be kept unto death.'

sentences.zh: 」乃流涕斬之。

translations.literal: Then weeping he executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Then, weeping, he executed him.

sentences.zh: 並收紹宗等屍，以禮埋瘞。

translations.literal: He also collected the bodies of Shaozong and others and buried them with rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also collected the bodies of Shaozong and the others and buried them with proper rites.

sentences.zh: 岳既失紹宗等，志氣沮喪，不敢逼城。

translations.literal: Yue, having lost Shaozong and others, was dispirited and dared not press the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, having lost Shaozong and the others, was dispirited and dared not press the city.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄聞之，乃率步騎十萬來攻。

translations.literal: When Gao Cheng of Qi heard this, he led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng of Qi heard of this, he led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to attack.

sentences.zh: 思政知不濟，率左右據土山，因仰天大哭，左右皆號慟。

translations.literal: Sizheng knew success was impossible; led attendants to hold an earthen mound and cried aloud to Heaven; attendants all wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng knew success was impossible, led his attendants to hold an earthen mound, and cried aloud to Heaven; his attendants all wailed in grief.

sentences.zh: 思政西向再拜，便欲自剄。

translations.literal: Sizheng bowed twice toward the west and was about to cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng bowed twice toward the west and was about to cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 先是，文襄告城中人曰：「有能生致王大將軍者，封侯重賞。

translations.literal: Earlier Gao Cheng had told the people in the city: 'Whoever can capture Grand General Wang alive will be enfeoffed and richly rewarded.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gao Cheng had told the people in the city, 'Whoever can capture Grand General Wang alive will be enfeoffed and richly rewarded.'

sentences.zh: 若大將軍身有損傷，親近左右皆從大戮。

translations.literal: If the Grand General's person is harmed, all those close to him will be put to death.'
translations.idiomatic: If the Grand General is harmed, all those close to him will be put to death.'

sentences.zh: 」都督駱訓固止之，不得引決。

translations.literal: The Commander Luo Xun firmly stopped him, and he could not take his life.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Luo Xun firmly stopped him, and he could not take his life.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄遣其通直散騎常侍趙彥深，就土山遺以白羽扇而說之，牽手以下。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng of Qi sent Regular Attendant Cavalier of Direct Transmission Zhao Yanshen to the earthen mound, presented a white feather fan and persuaded him, taking his hand to lead him down.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng of Qi sent his Regular Attendant Cavalier of Direct Transmission Zhao Yanshen to the earthen mound, presented a white feather fan, and persuaded him, taking his hand to lead him down.

sentences.zh: 引見文襄，辭氣慷慨，涕淚交流，無撓屈之容。

translations.literal: He was brought before Gao Cheng; his words were impassioned, tears streamed, and there was no appearance of submission.
translations.idiomatic: He was brought before Gao Cheng. His words were impassioned, tears streamed down his face, and there was no sign of submission.

sentences.zh: 文襄以其忠於所事，起而禮之，接遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng, because of his loyalty to his former master, rose and honored him and treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng, because of his loyalty to his former master, rose and honored him and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 其督將分禁諸州地牢。

translations.literal: His commanders and generals were imprisoned separately in dungeons across the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders and generals were imprisoned separately in dungeons across the provinces.

sentences.zh: 數年盡死。

translations.literal: Within several years they all died.
translations.idiomatic: Within several years they all died.

sentences.zh: 思政初入潁川，士卒八千人。

translations.literal: When Sizheng first entered Yingchuan, he had eight thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Sizheng first entered Yingchuan, he had eight thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 被圍既久，城中無鹽，腫死者十六七，及城陷之日，存者才三千人。

translations.literal: The siege had lasted long; there was no salt in the city, and six or seven out of ten died of swelling. On the day the city fell, only three thousand survived.
translations.idiomatic: The siege dragged on until the city ran out of salt; six or seven out of ten died of swelling. When the city finally fell, only three thousand were left alive.

sentences.zh: 雖外無救援，遂無叛者。

translations.literal: Though there was no relief from outside, there were no defectors.
translations.idiomatic: Though no relief came from outside, no one defected.

sentences.zh: 思政常以勤王為務，不營資產。

translations.literal: Sizheng always made rescuing the throne his task and did not pursue assets.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng always made rescuing the throne his priority and did not pursue personal wealth.

sentences.zh: 嘗被賜園地，思政出征後，家人種桑果雜樹。

translations.literal: Once he was granted an estate; after Sizheng went on campaign, his family planted mulberries, fruit trees, and assorted trees.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was granted an estate; after Sizheng went on campaign, his family planted mulberries, fruit trees, and other trees on it.

sentences.zh: 及還，見而怒曰：「匈奴未滅，去病辭家，況大賊未平，欲事產業，豈所謂憂公忘私邪！

translations.literal: On his return he saw this and angrily said: 'The Xiongnu were not yet destroyed when Huo Qubing left home; how much more when the great enemy is not yet pacified — to pursue an estate, is this what is meant by caring for the public and forgetting the private!'
translations.idiomatic: On his return he saw this and angrily said, 'Huo Qubing left home before the Xiongnu were destroyed; how much more now, with the great enemy still unbeaten, can you pursue an estate? Is this what caring for the public and forgetting the private means?'

sentences.zh: 」命左右拔而棄之。

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to pull them up and discard them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to pull them up and throw them away.

sentences.zh: 故身陷之後，家無蓄積。

translations.literal: Therefore after he was captured, his household had no savings.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore after he was captured, his household had no savings.

sentences.zh: 及齊文宣受東魏禪，以思政為都官尚書、儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Gao Yang of Qi accepted the abdication of Eastern Wei, he appointed Sizheng Director of the Ministry of Justice with third-rank honorary equivalence.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yang of Qi accepted the abdication of Eastern Wei, he made Sizheng Director of the Ministry of Justice with third-rank honorary equivalence.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈以本官，加兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted his former office plus the post of Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted his former office plus inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 初，思政在荊州，自武關以南延袤一千五百里，置三十餘城，並當沖要之地。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sizheng was in Jing Province, from Wuguan southward for fifteen hundred li he established more than thirty cities, all at strategically vital points.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Sizheng held Jing Province, he established more than thirty cities over fifteen hundred li south from Wuguan, all at strategically vital points.

sentences.zh: 凡所舉薦，咸得其才。

translations.literal: All those he recommended proved equal to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: Every man he recommended proved fit for the role.

sentences.zh: 子康，沈毅有度量，後為周文親信。

translations.literal: His son Kang was steady and resolute with breadth of mind and later became a trusted confidant of Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang was steady, resolute, and broad-minded, and later became one of Duke Wen's trusted confidants.

sentences.zh: 思政陷後，詔以因水城陷，非戰之罪，增邑三千五百戶，以康襲爵太原公，除驃騎大將軍、侍中、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: After Sizheng's capture, an edict held that the fall of the city by water was not a fault of battle, added three thousand five hundred households to the fief, had Kang inherit the title Duke of Taiyuan, and appointed him General of Agile Cavalry, Palace Attendant, and Opener of the Mansion with third-rank honorary equivalence.
translations.idiomatic: After Sizheng's capture, an edict held that the city's fall by flooding was not a fault in battle, added three thousand five hundred households to the fief, had Kang inherit the title Duke of Taiyuan, and appointed him General of Agile Cavalry, Palace Attendant, and Opener of the Mansion with third-rank honorary equivalence.

sentences.zh: 康弟揆，先封中都縣侯，增邑通前一千五百戶，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Kang's younger brother Kui had earlier been enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhongdu County; his fief was increased to one thousand five hundred households in all and he was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's younger brother Kui had earlier been enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhongdu County; his fief was increased to one thousand five hundred households in all and he was promoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 揆弟邗，封西安縣侯。

translations.literal: Kui's younger brother Han was enfeoffed Marquis of Xi'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's younger brother Han was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xi'an County.

sentences.zh: 邗弟恭，忠誠縣伯。

translations.literal: Han's younger brother Gong was Baron of Zhongcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Han's younger brother Gong was Baron of Zhongcheng County.

sentences.zh: 恭弟細，顯親縣伯。

translations.literal: Gong's younger brother Xi was Baron of Xianqin County.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's younger brother Xi was Baron of Xianqin County.

sentences.zh: 康姊封齊郡君。

translations.literal: Kang's elder sister was enfeoffed Lady of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's elder sister was enfeoffed as Lady of Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 康兄元遜亦陷於潁川，封其子景晉陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Kang's elder brother Yuansun also fell at Yingchuan; his son Jing was enfeoffed Marquis of Jinyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's elder brother Yuansun also fell at Yingchuan, and his son Jing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jinyang County.

sentences.zh: 康抗表固讓，不許。

translations.literal: Kang submitted a memorial firmly declining, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Kang submitted a memorial firmly declining the honor, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 十六年，王師東討，加康使持節、大都督，以思政所部兵皆配之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the royal army marched east; Kang was given the Staff of Authority and made Grand Commander, and all troops under Sizheng were assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the royal army marched east; Kang was given the Staff of Authority and made grand commander, and all troops under Sizheng were assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，隨尉遲迥征蜀，鎮天水郡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei he followed Wei Chijiong on the Shu campaign and was stationed at Tianshui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei he followed Wei Chijiong on the Shu campaign and was posted to Tianshui Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋賜姓拓王氏。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted the surname Tuo and clan name Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was granted the surname Tuo and the clan name Wang.

sentences.zh: 為鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Inspector of Fu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as inspector of Fu Province.

sentences.zh: 武成末，除匠師中大夫，轉載師。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wucheng era he was appointed Grand Master of Craftsmen and transferred to Grand Master of Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wucheng era he was appointed Grand Master of Craftsmen and then transferred to Grand Master of Carriages.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，曆安、襄二州總管，位柱國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding he served in succession as Commander of An and Xiang provinces and held the rank of Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding he served in succession as commander of An and Xiang provinces and held the rank of Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 入隋，終於汴州刺史。

translations.literal: Under the Sui he ended his career as Inspector of Bian Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he ended his career as inspector of Bian Province.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥，字薄居羅，代人也。

translations.literal: Wei Chijiong, courtesy name Bojuluo, was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chijiong, whose courtesy name was Bojuluo, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其先，魏之別種，號尉遲部，因而氏焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors were a separate branch of Wei, called the Wei Chi tribe, and from this they took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were a separate branch of the Wei people called the Wei Chi tribe, from which they took their surname.

sentences.zh: 父俟兜，性弘裕有鑒識，尚周文帝姊昌樂大長公主，生迥及綱。

translations.literal: His father Qidou was broad-minded and discerning by nature, married the elder sister of Duke Wen of Zhou, the Grand Princess of Changle, and fathered Chijiong and Gang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qidou was broad-minded and discerning. He married Duke Wen of Zhou's elder sister, the Grand Princess of Changle, and fathered Chijiong and Gang.

sentences.zh: 迥年七歲，綱年六歲，俟兜病且卒，呼二子，撫其首曰：「汝等並有貴相，但恨吾不見耳，各勉之。

translations.literal: Chijiong was seven and Gang six when Qidou fell ill and was near death. He called the two boys, stroked their heads, and said: 'You both have noble countenances, but I regret I shall not see it — each of you strive hard.'
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong was seven and Gang six when Qidou fell mortally ill. He called the two boys, stroked their heads, and said, 'You both have noble countenances, but I regret I shall not live to see it — each of you strive hard.'

sentences.zh: 」武成初，追贈柱國大將軍、太傅、長樂郡公，諡曰定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng he was posthumously granted Pillar of the State, Grand General, Grand Tutor, Duke of Changle Commandery, posthumous name Settled.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng he was posthumously granted Pillar of the State, Grand General, Grand Tutor, and Duke of Changle Commandery, with the posthumous name Settled.

sentences.zh: 迥少聰敏，美容儀。

translations.literal: Chijiong was clever and quick as a youth and handsome in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Chijiong was clever and handsome in bearing.

sentences.zh: 及長，有大志，好施愛士。

translations.literal: When he grew up he had great ambition, loved to give, and cherished scholars.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he had great ambition, loved to give, and cherished men of talent.

sentences.zh: 尚魏文帝女金明公主，拜駙馬都尉，封西都侯。

translations.literal: He married the daughter of Emperor Wen of Wei, Princess Jinming, was appointed Commandant of the Horse for the Son-in-Law, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xidu.
translations.idiomatic: He married Emperor Wen of Wei's daughter, Princess Jinming, was appointed Commandant of the Horse for the Son-in-Law, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xidu.

sentences.zh: 大統十一年，拜侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵魏安郡公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dazong he was appointed Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Opener of the Mansion with third-rank honorary equivalence, and advanced to Duke of Wei'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Dazong he was appointed Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Opener of the Mansion with third-rank honorary equivalence, and promoted to Duke of Wei'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷尚書左僕射，兼領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently made General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently made General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 迥通敏有幹能，雖任兼文武，頗允時望，周文以此深委仗焉。

translations.literal: Chijiong was quick, perceptive, and capable; though his duties combined civil and military roles, he largely met the expectations of the age, and Duke Wen for this reason deeply entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong was quick, perceptive, and capable. Though his duties combined civil and military roles, he largely met public expectations, and Duke Wen deeply entrusted him for that reason.

sentences.zh: 十六年，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 侯景之渡江也，梁元帝時鎮江陵，請修鄰好。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi, Emperor Yuan of Liang was then stationed at Jiangling and requested friendly relations with his neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi, Emperor Yuan of Liang was stationed at Jiangling and requested friendly relations with his neighbor.

sentences.zh: 其弟武陵王紀在蜀稱帝，率眾東下，將攻之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Prince of Wuling Ji had declared himself emperor in Shu, led troops eastward, and was about to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Prince of Wuling Ji had declared himself emperor in Shu, led his forces eastward, and was about to attack him.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝大懼，移書請救。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang was greatly afraid and sent a letter requesting rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang was greatly afraid and sent a letter requesting rescue.

sentences.zh: 周文曰：「蜀可圖矣！

translations.literal: Duke Wen said: 'Shu can be taken!'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen said, 'Shu can be taken!'

sentences.zh: 取蜀制梁，在茲一舉。

translations.literal: To take Shu and control Liang depends on this one move.
translations.idiomatic: To take Shu and control Liang depends on this one move.'

sentences.zh: 」乃與群公會議，諸將多有異同。

translations.literal: Then he met with the nobles in council; the generals were much divided in opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Then he met with the nobles in council, and the generals were much divided in opinion.

sentences.zh: 唯迥以為紀既盡銳東下，蜀必空虛，王師臨之，必有征無戰。

translations.literal: Only Chijiong held that since Ji had committed all his elite forces eastward, Shu must be empty, and when the royal army arrived there would be conquest without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Only Chijiong argued that since Ji had committed all his elite forces eastward, Shu must be empty, and when the royal army arrived there would be conquest without battle.

sentences.zh: 周文以為然，謂曰：「伐蜀之事，一以委汝。

translations.literal: Duke Wen agreed and said to him: 'The matter of attacking Shu I entrust entirely to you.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen agreed and told him, 'The matter of attacking Shu I entrust entirely to you.'

sentences.zh: 」於是令迥督開府元珍、乙弗亞、侯呂陵始、叱奴興、綦連雄、宇文升等六軍甲士取晉壽，開平林舊道。

translations.literal: Then he ordered Chijiong to command six armies of armored troops under Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya, Hou Lülingshi, Cinu Xing, Qilian Xiong, Yuwen Sheng, and others to take Jinshou by the old Pinglin route.
translations.idiomatic: Then he ordered Chijiong to command six armies of armored troops under Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya, Hou Lülingshi, Cinu Xing, Qilian Xiong, Yuwen Sheng, and others to take Jinshou by the old Pinglin route.

sentences.zh: 迥前軍臨劍閣，紀安州刺史樂廣以州先降。

translations.literal: Chijiong's vanguard reached Jiange, and Yue Guang, Ji's Inspector of An Province, surrendered the province first.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong's vanguard reached Jiange, and Yue Guang, Ji's inspector of An Province, surrendered the province first.

sentences.zh: 紀梁州刺史楊乾運時鎮潼水，先已遣使詣闕，密送誠款，然恐其下不從，猶據潼水別營拒守。

translations.literal: Yang Qianyun, Ji's Inspector of Liang Province, was then stationed at Tongshui. He had already sent envoys to court with secret pledges of loyalty, but fearing his subordinates would not follow, he still held a separate camp at Tongshui in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qianyun, Ji's inspector of Liang Province, was then stationed at Tongshui. He had already sent envoys to court with secret pledges of loyalty, but fearing his subordinates would not follow, he still held a separate camp at Tongshui in defense.

sentences.zh: 迥遣元珍、侯呂陵始等襲之，乾運還保潼川。

translations.literal: Chijiong sent Yuan Zhen, Hou Lülingshi, and others to raid him; Qianyun withdrew to defend Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong sent Yuan Zhen, Hou Lülingshi, and others to attack him, and Qianyun withdrew to defend Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 珍等遂圍之，乾運降。

translations.literal: Zhen and others then besieged him; Qianyun surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and the others then besieged him, and Qianyun surrendered.

sentences.zh: 迥至潼川，大餉將士，度涪江，至青溪，登南原，勒兵講武，修繕約束，閱器械，自開府以下賞金帛各有差。

translations.literal: When Chijiong reached Tongchuan he feasted the officers and soldiers generously, crossed the Fu River, reached Qingxi, ascended the southern plain, drilled the troops and reviewed martial arts, repaired discipline, inspected weapons, and rewarded gold and silk in differing amounts from Opener of the Mansion downward.
translations.idiomatic: When Chijiong reached Tongchuan he feasted his officers and men generously, crossed the Fu River, reached Qingxi, ascended the southern plain, drilled the troops, restored discipline, inspected weapons, and rewarded gold and silk in differing amounts from Opener of the Mansion downward.

sentences.zh: 時夏中連雨，山路險峻，將士疲病者十二三，迥親自勞問，加以湯藥，引之而西。

translations.literal: At the time it rained continuously in midsummer, the mountain roads were steep and dangerous, and one or two out of ten officers and soldiers were exhausted or ill. Chijiong personally comforted them, gave them medicine, and led them westward.
translations.idiomatic: It rained continuously in midsummer, the mountain roads were steep and dangerous, and one or two out of ten officers and men were exhausted or ill. Chijiong personally comforted them, gave them medicine, and led them westward.

sentences.zh: 紀益州刺史蕭捴嬰城自守，進軍圍之。

translations.literal: Xiao Chou, Ji's Inspector of Yi Province, closed the city and defended himself, and Chijiong advanced and besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chou, Ji's inspector of Yi Province, closed the city and defended himself, and Chijiong advanced and besieged him.

sentences.zh: 初，紀至巴郡，遣前南梁州刺史史欣景、幽州刺史趙拔扈等為捴外援。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ji reached Ba Commandery, he sent the former Inspector of South Liang Province Shi Xinjing, Inspector of You Province Zhao Bahu, and others as external aid to Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ji reached Ba Commandery, he sent the former inspector of South Liang Province Shi Xinjing, inspector of You Province Zhao Bahu, and others as external aid to Chou.

sentences.zh: 迥分遣元珍、乙弗亞等擊破之。

translations.literal: Chijiong sent Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya, and others in separate detachments to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong sent Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya, and others in separate detachments to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 拔扈等遁走，欣景遂降。

translations.literal: Bahu and others fled; Xinjing then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Bahu and the others fled, and Xinjing then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 捴被圍五旬，頻戰為迥所破。

translations.literal: Chou was besieged fifty days and was repeatedly defeated in battle by Chijiong.
translations.idiomatic: Chou was besieged for fifty days and was repeatedly defeated in battle by Chijiong.

sentences.zh: 遣使乞降，許之。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy to beg surrender, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an envoy to beg surrender, and Chijiong granted it.

sentences.zh: 捴乃與紀子宜都王圓肅率其文武詣軍門請見，迥以禮接之。

translations.literal: Chou then came with Ji's son Prince of Yidu Yuan Su and civil and military officials to the camp gate to request audience; Chijiong received them with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Chou then came with Ji's son Prince of Yidu Yuan Su and their civil and military officials to the camp gate to request an audience, and Chijiong received them with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 其吏人等各令復業，唯收僮隸及儲積以賞將士。

translations.literal: He ordered the officials and people each to resume their occupations, taking only servants and stored goods to reward the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the officials and people each to resume their occupations, taking only servants and stored goods to reward his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 號令嚴肅，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: Orders were strict and solemn; the army had no private gains.
translations.idiomatic: His orders were strict and solemn, and the army took no private gains.

sentences.zh: 詔以迥為大都督、益潼等十二州諸軍事、益州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Chijiong Grand Commander, Commander of military affairs of twelve provinces including Yi and Tong, and Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Chijiong grand commander, commander of military affairs of twelve provinces including Yi and Tong, and inspector of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 三年，加督六州，通前十八州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the third year six more provinces were added to his command, for eighteen provinces' military affairs in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year six more provinces were added to his command, for eighteen provinces' military affairs in all.

sentences.zh: 以平蜀功，封一子安固郡公。

translations.literal: For the merit of pacifying Shu, one of his sons was enfeoffed as Duke of Angu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Shu, one of his sons was enfeoffed as Duke of Angu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 自劍閣以南得承制封拜及黜陟。
