translations.literal: From Jiange southward he was empowered to enfeoff, appoint, dismiss, and promote by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiange southward he was empowered to enfeoff, appoint, dismiss, and promote by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 迥乃明賞罰，布恩威，綏輯新邦，經略未附，人夷懷而歸之。

translations.literal: Chijiong then made rewards and punishments clear, spread favor and authority, pacified the new territory, brought strategy to those not yet attached; Chinese and barbarians came to him in goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong then made rewards and punishments clear, spread favor and authority, pacified the new territory, brought strategy to those not yet attached, and both Chinese and barbarians came to him in goodwill.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，色養不怠，身雖在外，所得四時甘脆，必先薦奉，然後敢嘗。

translations.literal: By nature he was deeply filial and never slack in attending to parents' comfort; though away, seasonal delicacies he always offered first and only then dared taste.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was deeply filial and never slack in attending to his parents' comfort. Though he was away, whenever he obtained seasonal delicacies he always offered them first and only then dared to taste them.

sentences.zh: 大長公主年高多病，迥往在京師，每退朝參候起居，憂悴形于容色。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess was advanced in years and often ill; when Chijiong was in the capital he visited after every court session to inquire after her health; worry showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess was advanced in years and often ill. When Chijiong was in the capital he visited her after every court session to inquire after her health, and worry showed in his face.

sentences.zh: 大長公主每為之和顏進食，以寧迥心。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess each time composed her expression and urged him to eat, to settle Chijiong's heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess each time would compose her expression and urge him to eat, to settle Chijiong's heart.

sentences.zh: 周文知其至性，征迥入朝，以慰其母意。

translations.literal: Duke Wen, knowing his deep nature, summoned Chijiong to court to comfort his mother's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen, knowing his deep filial nature, summoned Chijiong to court to comfort his mother.

sentences.zh: 遣大鴻臚郊勞，仍賜迥袞冕之服。

translations.literal: He sent the Grand Master of Hospitality to welcome at the outskirts and also granted Chijiong robes of highest ceremonial rank.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Grand Master of Hospitality to welcome him at the outskirts and also granted Chijiong robes of the highest ceremonial rank.

sentences.zh: 蜀人思之，為立碑頌德。

translations.literal: The people of Shu missed him and erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu missed him and erected a stele praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 六官初建，拜小宗伯。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were first established he was appointed Lesser Minister of the Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were first established, he was appointed Lesser Minister of the Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，進位柱國大將軍，以迥有平蜀功，同霍去病冠軍之義，改封寧蜀公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Chijiong was advanced to Pillar of the State and Grand General. Because Chijiong had the merit of pacifying Shu, in the same sense as Huo Qubing's title Conqueror of the Enemy, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Ningshu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Chijiong was advanced to Pillar of the State and Grand General. Because he had pacified Shu, in the same sense as Huo Qubing's title Conqueror of the Enemy, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Ningshu.

sentences.zh: 遷大司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官鎮隴右。

translations.literal: Soon he was stationed at Longyou with his existing office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posted to Longyou with his existing office.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，進封蜀國公，邑萬戶，除秦州總管、秦渭等十四州諸軍事、隴右大都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng he was advanced to Duke of the State of Shu with a fief of ten thousand households, appointed Commander of Qin Province, Commander of military affairs of fourteen provinces including Qin and Wei, and Grand Commander of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wucheng he was promoted to Duke of the State of Shu with a fief of ten thousand households, appointed commander of Qin Province, commander of military affairs of fourteen provinces including Qin and Wei, and grand commander of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，拜大司馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding he was appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding he was appointed Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 及晉公護東伐，迥帥師攻洛陽。

translations.literal: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu marched east, Chijiong led troops to attack Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu marched east, Chijiong led troops to attack Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲等軍於芒山，齊眾度河，諸軍驚散。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian and others were encamped at Mangshan when Qi forces crossed the river and the armies scattered in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian and others were encamped at Mangshan when Qi forces crossed the river and the armies scattered in alarm.

sentences.zh: 迥率麾下反行卻敵，於是諸將遂得全師而還。

translations.literal: Chijiong led his followers in a countermarch to repel the enemy; thus the generals were able to bring armies back intact.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong led his followers in a countermarch to repel the enemy, and thus the generals were able to bring their armies back intact.

sentences.zh: 遷太保、太傅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Guardian and Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Guardian and Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 建德初，拜太師，尋加上柱國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande he was appointed Grand Preceptor and soon given added rank Upper Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianade he was appointed Grand Preceptor and soon given the added rank of Upper Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，以迥為大右弼，轉大前疑，出為相州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he made Chijiong Great Right Assistant, then transferred him to Great Forward Doubter and sent him out as Commander of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he made Chijiong Great Right Assistant, then transferred him to Great Forward Doubter and sent him out as commander of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 宣帝崩，隋文帝輔政，以迥位望宿重，懼為異圖，乃令迥子魏安郡公惇齎詔書以會葬征迥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Emperor Wen of Sui served as regent; because Chijiong's rank and reputation were long established and he feared other designs, he ordered Chijiong's son Dun, Duke of Wei'an Commandery, to bring an imperial edict summoning Chijiong to the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan died, Emperor Wen of Sui served as regent. Because Chijiong's rank and reputation were long established and he feared other designs, he ordered Chijiong's son Dun, Duke of Wei'an Commandery, to bring an imperial edict summoning Chijiong to the funeral.

sentences.zh: 尋以鄖國公韋孝寬代迥為總管。

translations.literal: Soon Duke of Yun Wei Xiaokuan was sent to replace Chijiong as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Duke of Yun Wei Xiaokuan was sent to replace Chijiong as commander.

sentences.zh: 迥以隋文帝當權，將圖篡奪，遂謀舉兵，留惇而不受代。

translations.literal: Chijiong, believing Emperor Wen of Sui held power and intended usurpation, then plotted to raise troops, kept Dun with him, and refused replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong, believing that Emperor Wen of Sui held power and intended usurpation, then plotted to raise troops, kept Dun with him, and refused replacement.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝又令候正破六韓裒詣迥喻旨，密與總管府長史晉昶等書，令為之備。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui also sent Hou Zheng Pohou Han'ai to Chijiong to explain the court's intent, and secretly wrote to chief administrator Jin Chang and others to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui also sent Hou Zheng Pohou Han'ai to Chijiong to explain the court's intent, and secretly wrote to the chief administrator of the commandery office Jin Chang and others to prepare.

sentences.zh: 迥聞之，殺昶，集文武士庶等登城北樓而令之。

translations.literal: When Chijiong heard of this he killed Chang, gathered civil and military officials and commoners, ascended the north gate tower, and issued orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Chijiong heard of this he killed Chang, gathered civil and military officials and commoners, ascended the north gate tower, and issued his orders.

sentences.zh: 於是眾咸從命，莫不感激。

translations.literal: Then the multitude all obeyed; none failed to be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Then the multitude all obeyed, and none failed to be moved.

sentences.zh: 乃自稱大總管，承制署官司。

translations.literal: He then styled himself Grand Commander and by imperial commission appointed officials and offices.
translations.idiomatic: He then styled himself Grand Commander and by imperial commission appointed officials and offices.

sentences.zh: 于時趙王招已入朝，留少子在國，迥又奉以號令。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Zhao Zhao had already entered court and left a younger son in the domain; Chijiong also upheld him in issuing orders.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Zhao Zhao had already entered court and left a younger son in the domain, and Chijiong also upheld him in issuing orders.

sentences.zh: 迥弟子大將軍、成平郡公勤時為青州總管，初得迥書表送之，尋亦從迥。

translations.literal: Chijiong's nephew Qin, Grand General and Duke of Chengping Commandery, was then Commander of Qing Province. At first, on receiving Chijiong's letter he submitted it to court, but soon he followed Chijiong as well.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong's nephew Qin, Grand General and Duke of Chengping Commandery, was then commander of Qing Province. At first, on receiving Chijiong's letter he submitted it to court, but soon he followed Chijiong as well.

sentences.zh: 迥所管相、衛、黎、毛、洺、貝、趙、冀、瀛、滄，勤所統青、齊、膠、光、莒諸州皆從之，眾數十萬。

translations.literal: Provinces under Chijiong — Xiang, Wei, Li, Mao, Ming, Bei, Zhao, Ji, Ying, Cang — and provinces under Qin — Qing, Qi, Jiao, Guang, Ju — all followed, numbering several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces under Chijiong — Xiang, Wei, Li, Mao, Ming, Bei, Zhao, Ji, Ying, and Cang — and the provinces under Qin — Qing, Qi, Jiao, Guang, and Ju — all followed him, numbering several hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 滎州刺史邵國公宇文胄、申州刺史李惠、東楚州刺史費也利進國、東潼州刺史曹孝達各據州以應迥。

translations.literal: Yuwen Zhou, Inspector of Ying Province and Duke of Shaoguo; Li Hui, Inspector of Shen Province; Fei Yelijingguo, Inspector of East Chu Province; and Cao Xiaoda, Inspector of East Tong Province each held their provinces in response to Chijiong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhou, inspector of Ying Province and Duke of Shaoguo; Li Hui, inspector of Shen Province; Fei Yelijingguo, inspector of East Chu Province; and Cao Xiaoda, inspector of East Tong Province each held their provinces in response to Chijiong.

sentences.zh: 徐州總管司錄席毗與前東平郡守畢義緒據兗州及徐州之蘭陵郡，亦以應迥。

translations.literal: Xi Pi, Chief Clerk of the Xuzhou commandery office, and Bi Yixu, former Administrator of Dongping Commandery, held Yan Province and Lanling Commandery of Xuzhou and also responded to Chijiong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Pi, chief clerk of the Xuzhou commandery office, and Bi Yixu, former administrator of Dongping Commandery, held Yan Province and Lanling Commandery of Xuzhou and also responded to Chijiong.

sentences.zh: 永橋鎮將紇豆陵惠以城降迥。

translations.literal: Hedouling Hui, garrison commander of Yongqiao, surrendered the city to Chijiong.
translations.idiomatic: Hedouling Hui, garrison commander of Yongqiao, surrendered the city to Chijiong.

sentences.zh: 迥又北結高寶寧以通突厥；

translations.literal: Chijiong also allied in the north with Gao Baoning to communicate with the Turks;
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong also allied in the north with Gao Baoning to communicate with the Turks;

sentences.zh: 南連陳人，許割江淮之地。

translations.literal: In the south he allied with Chen and promised to cede the lands of the Jianghuai.
translations.idiomatic: In the south he allied with Chen and promised to cede the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝於是徵兵討迥，即以韋孝寬為元帥，陰羅雲監諸軍，郕國公梁士彥、樂安西元諧、化政公宇文忻、濮陽公宇文述、武鄉公崔弘度、清河公楊素、隴西公李詢、延壽公于仲文等皆為行軍總管。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui then mobilized troops to attack Chijiong, appointing Wei Xiaokuan as commander-in-chief, Yin Luoyun to oversee the armies, and Liang Shiyan Duke of Yingguo, Yuan Xie of Le'anxi, Yuwen Xin Duke of Huazheng, Yuwen Shu Duke of Puyang, Cui Hongdu Duke of Wuxiang, Yang Su Duke of Qinghe, Li Xun Duke of Longxi, and Yu Zhongwen Duke of Yanshou as campaign commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui then mobilized troops against Chijiong, making Wei Xiaokuan commander-in-chief, Yin Luoyun overseer of the armies, and Liang Shiyan, Yuan Xie, Yuwen Xin, Yuwen Shu, Cui Hongdu, Yang Su, Li Xun, and Yu Zhongwen campaign commanders.

sentences.zh: 迥遣所署大將軍石愻攻建州，刺史宇文弁以州降愻。

translations.literal: Chijiong sent his appointed Grand General Shi Sun to attack Jian Province, and the Inspector Yuwen Bian surrendered the province to Sun.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong sent his appointed Grand General Shi Sun to attack Jian Province, and Inspector Yuwen Bian surrendered the province to him.

sentences.zh: 迥又遣西道行台韓長業攻陷潞州，執刺史趙威，署城人郭子勝為刺史。

translations.literal: Chijiong also sent the Western Route Commissioner Han Changye to capture Lu Province, seized the Inspector Zhao Wei, and appointed the townsman Guo Zisheng as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong also sent Western Route Commissioner Han Changye to capture Lu Province, seized Inspector Zhao Wei, and appointed the townsman Guo Zisheng as inspector.

sentences.zh: 上儀同赫連士猷攻晉州，即據小鄉城。

translations.literal: Helian Shiyou with upper third-rank honorary equivalence attacked Jin Province and immediately seized Xiaoxiang city.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Shiyou with upper third-rank honorary equivalence attacked Jin Province and immediately seized Xiaoxiang city.

sentences.zh: 紇豆陵惠襲陷定州之钜鹿郡，遂圍恆州。

translations.literal: Hedouling Hui raided and captured Julu Commandery of Ding Province, then besieged Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Hedouling Hui raided and captured Julu Commandery of Ding Province, then besieged Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 上大將軍宇文威攻汴州，上開府莒州刺史烏丸尼、開府尉遲俊率膠、光、青、齊、莒、兗之眾圍沂州。

translations.literal: Yuwen Wei, Upper Grand General, attacked Bian Province; Wuyan Ni, Inspector of Ju Province and Upper Opener of the Mansion, and Yuwen Jun, Opener of the Mansion, led the forces of Jiao, Guang, Qing, Qi, Ju, and Yan to besiege Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Upper Grand General Yuwen Wei attacked Bian Province; Upper Opener of the Mansion Wuyan Ni, Inspector of Ju Province, and Opener of the Mansion Yuwen Jun led forces from Jiao, Guang, Qing, Qi, Ju, and Yan to besiege Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 大將軍檀讓攻陷曹、亳二州，屯兵梁郡。

translations.literal: Grand General Tan Rang captured Cao and Bo provinces and encamped at Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Tan Rang captured Cao and Bo provinces and encamped at Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 大將軍、東南道行台席毗眾號八萬，軍於籓城，攻陷昌慮、下邑、豐縣。

translations.literal: Grand General and Southeast Route Commissioner Xi Pi, force said to number eighty thousand, encamped at Fancheng and captured Changlu, Xiayi, and Feng County.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General and Southeast Route Commissioner Xi Pi, whose force was said to number eighty thousand, encamped at Fancheng and captured Changlu, Xiayi, and Feng County.

sentences.zh: 李惠自申州攻永州，焚之而還。

translations.literal: Li Hui attacked Yong Province from Shen Province, burned it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui attacked Yong Province from Shen Province, burned it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宇文胄軍於洛口。

translations.literal: Yuwen Zhou encamped at Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhou encamped at Luokou.

sentences.zh: 開府梁子康攻懷州。

translations.literal: Liang Zikang, Opener of the Mansion, attacked Huai Province.
translations.idiomatic: Opener of the Mansion Liang Zikang attacked Huai Province.

sentences.zh: 魏安公惇率眾十萬人入武德，軍於沁東。

translations.literal: Dun, Duke of Wei'an, led one hundred thousand men into Wude and encamped east of the Qin River.
translations.idiomatic: Dun, Duke of Wei'an, led one hundred thousand men into Wude and encamped east of the Qin River.

sentences.zh: 孝寬等諸軍隔水，相持不進。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan and the other armies faced each other across the water and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan and the other armies faced each other across the water and neither side advanced.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝又遣高熲馳驛督戰。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui also sent Gao Jiong by express post to supervise the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui also sent Gao Jiong by express post to supervise the battle.

sentences.zh: 惇布兵二十餘里，麾軍小卻，欲待孝寬軍半度而擊之。

translations.literal: Dun deployed his troops for more than twenty li, ordered the army to fall back slightly, and intended to strike when Xiaokuan's army was half across.
translations.idiomatic: Dun deployed his troops for more than twenty li, ordered a slight withdrawal, and intended to strike when Xiaokuan's army was half across.

sentences.zh: 孝寬因其卻，乃鳴鼓齊進，惇遂大敗。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan, taking advantage of the withdrawal, beat drums and advanced together; Dun was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan, taking advantage of the withdrawal, beat the drums and advanced together, and Dun was utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乘勝進至鄴，迥與其子惇、佑等又悉其卒十三萬，陣于城南。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan pressed the victory to Ye. Chijiong with his sons Dun, You, and the others again mustered all one hundred thirty thousand soldiers and formed battle lines south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan pressed the victory to Ye. Chijiong with his sons Dun, You, and the others mustered all one hundred thirty thousand soldiers and formed battle lines south of the city.

sentences.zh: 迥別統萬人，皆綠巾錦襖，號曰黃龍兵。

translations.literal: Chijiong separately commanded ten thousand men, all with green headcloths and brocade jackets, called Yellow Dragon troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong separately commanded ten thousand men, all with green headcloths and brocade jackets, called the Yellow Dragon troops.

sentences.zh: 勤率眾五萬自青州赴迥，以三千騎先到。

translations.literal: Qin led fifty thousand men from Qing Province to join Chijiong, with three thousand horsemen arriving first.
translations.idiomatic: Qin led fifty thousand men from Qing Province to join Chijiong; three thousand horsemen arrived first.

sentences.zh: 迥舊集軍旅，雖老，猶被甲臨陣。

translations.literal: Chijiong had long gathered armies; though old, he still donned armor and went to the front.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong had long commanded armies; though old, he still donned armor and went to the front.

sentences.zh: 其麾下兵皆關中人，為之力戰。

translations.literal: The soldiers under his command were all men of Guanzhong and fought fiercely for him.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers were all men of Guanzhong and fought fiercely for him.

sentences.zh: 孝寬等軍失利而卻。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan's army and the others were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan's army was defeated and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 鄴中士女觀者如堵。

translations.literal: The men and women of Ye who watched were packed like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: The men and women of Ye who watched were packed shoulder to shoulder.

sentences.zh: 高熲與李詢乃整陣先犯觀者，因其擾而乘之。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong and Li Xun then formed ranks and first charged the spectators, then took advantage of the disturbance to press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong and Li Xun formed ranks and first charged the spectators, then took advantage of the disturbance to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 迥眾大敗，遂入鄴城。

translations.literal: Chijiong's forces were utterly defeated and fled into Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong's forces were utterly defeated and fled into Ye.

sentences.zh: 迥走保北城，孝寬縱兵圍之。

translations.literal: Chijiong fled to hold the north city; Xiaokuan unleashed troops to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong fled to hold the north city, and Xiaokuan unleashed his troops to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 李詢、賀婁子幹以其屬先登。

translations.literal: Li Xun and Helou Zigan with their followers were the first to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun and Helou Zigan with their followers were the first to scale the wall.

sentences.zh: 迥上樓，射殺數人，乃自殺。

translations.literal: Chijiong went up a tower, shot and killed several men, then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong went up a tower, shot and killed several men, then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 勤、惇、佑等東走青州，未至，開府郭衍追及之，並為衍所獲。

translations.literal: Qin, Dun, You, and the others fled east toward Qing Province. Before they arrived, Guo Yan, Opener of the Mansion, overtook them and they were all captured by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Qin, Dun, You, and the others fled east toward Qing Province. Before they arrived, Opener of the Mansion Guo Yan overtook them and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝以勤初有誠款，特釋之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui, because Qin had at first shown sincerity, specially released him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui, because Qin had at first shown sincerity, specially released him.

sentences.zh: 李惠先是自縛歸罪，隋文帝復其官爵。

translations.literal: Li Hui had earlier bound himself and surrendered to accept guilt; Emperor Wen of Sui restored his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui had earlier bound himself and surrendered to accept guilt, and Emperor Wen of Sui restored his office and rank.

sentences.zh: 迥末年衰耄，惑于後妻王氏，而諸子多不睦。

translations.literal: In his later years Chijiong was aged and senile, deluded by his later wife Lady Wang, and his sons were mostly at odds.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Chijiong was aged and senile, deluded by his later wife Lady Wang, and his sons were mostly at odds with one another.

sentences.zh: 及起兵，以開府、小禦正崔達拏為長史，自餘委任，亦多用齊人。

translations.literal: When he raised troops he made Cui Dana, Opener of the Mansion and Lesser Director of the Palace Guard, chief administrator, and in other appointments also used many men of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When he raised troops he made Opener of the Mansion Cui Dana chief administrator, and in other appointments also used many men of Qi.

sentences.zh: 達拏文士，無籌略，舉措多失綱紀，不能匡救。

translations.literal: Dana was a literary man without strategy; his actions often violated discipline and he could not set things right.
translations.idiomatic: Dana was a literary man without strategic talent; his actions often violated discipline and he could not set things right.

sentences.zh: 迥自起兵至於敗，凡經六十八日焉。

translations.literal: From Chijiong's raising troops to his defeat, sixty-eight days in all had passed.
translations.idiomatic: From the raising of troops to defeat, Chijiong's rebellion lasted sixty-eight days in all.

sentences.zh: 子寬，大將軍、長樂郡公，先迥卒。

translations.literal: His son Kuan, Grand General and Duke of Changle Commandery, died before Chijiong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuan, Grand General and Duke of Changle Commandery, died before Chijiong.

sentences.zh: 寬兄誼，開府、資中郡公。

translations.literal: Kuan's elder brother Yi, Opener of the Mansion and Duke of Zizhong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's elder brother Yi was Opener of the Mansion and Duke of Zizhong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 寬弟順，以迥平蜀功，授開府、安固郡公。

translations.literal: Kuan's younger brother Shun, for Chijiong's merit in pacifying Shu, was granted Opener of the Mansion and Duke of Angu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's younger brother Shun, for Chijiong's merit in pacifying Shu, was granted Opener of the Mansion and Duke of Angu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後以女為宣帝皇后，拜上柱國，封胙國公。

translations.literal: Later because his daughter became Empress to Emperor Xuan, he was appointed Upper Pillar of the State and enfeoffed Duke of the State of Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because his daughter became Empress to Emperor Xuan, he was appointed Upper Pillar of the State and enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Zuo.

sentences.zh: 順弟惇，軍正下大夫、魏安郡公。

translations.literal: Shun's younger brother Dun, Grand Master of the Army Inspectorate and Duke of Wei'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's younger brother Dun was Grand Master of the Army Inspectorate and Duke of Wei'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 惇弟佑耆，西都郡公。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Youqi, Duke of Xidu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Youqi was Duke of Xidu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 皆被誅，而誼等諸子以年幼，並獲全。

translations.literal: All were executed; but Yi's sons and others, being young, were all spared.
translations.idiomatic: All were executed, but Yi's sons and the others, being young, were all spared.

sentences.zh: 武德中，迥從孫庫部員外郎耆福上表請改葬。

translations.literal: In the Wude era Chijiong's grand-nephew Qifu, Supernumerary Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue, submitted a memorial requesting reburial.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era Chijiong's grand-nephew Qifu, Supernumerary Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue, submitted a memorial requesting reburial.

sentences.zh: 朝議以迥忠於周室，有詔許焉，仍贈絹百匹。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held that Chijiong had been loyal to the house of Zhou, and an edict permitted it and additionally granted one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that Chijiong had been loyal to the house of Zhou, and an edict permitted the reburial and additionally granted one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 迥弟綱。

translations.literal: Chijiong's younger brother Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Chijiong's younger brother was Gang.

sentences.zh: 綱字婆羅，少孤，與兄迥依託舅氏。

translations.literal: Gang, courtesy name Poluo, was orphaned young and, with his elder brother Chijiong, relied on their mother's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Gang, whose courtesy name was Poluo, was orphaned young and, with his elder brother Chijiong, relied on their mother's clan.

sentences.zh: 周文帝西討關隴，迥、綱與母昌樂大長公主留于晉陽。

translations.literal: When Duke Wen of Zhou marched west against Guanlong, Chijiong, Gang, and their mother the Grand Princess of Changle remained at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Wen of Zhou marched west against Guanlong, Chijiong, Gang, and their mother the Grand Princess of Changle remained at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 後方入關。

translations.literal: Only afterward did they enter the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Only afterward did they enter the Pass.

sentences.zh: 從周文征伐，常陪侍帷幄，出入臥內。

translations.literal: He followed Duke Wen on campaigns, constantly attending in the command tent and entering and leaving his bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Duke Wen on campaigns, constantly attending in the command tent and entering and leaving his bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 以軍功封廣宗縣伯。

translations.literal: For military merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Guangzong County.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangzong County.

sentences.zh: 綱驍果有膂力，善騎射，周文甚寵之，委以心膂。

translations.literal: Gang was bold and resolute with great strength, skilled in horsemanship and archery. Duke Wen greatly favored him and entrusted him as a pillar of his rule.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was bold and resolute with great strength, skilled in horsemanship and archery. Duke Wen greatly favored him and entrusted him as a close confidant.

sentences.zh: 河橋之戰，周文馬中流矢，因而驚奔。

translations.literal: At the battle of Heqiao Duke Wen's horse was struck by a flying arrow and bolted in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Heqiao Duke Wen's horse was struck by a flying arrow and bolted in alarm.

sentences.zh: 綱與李穆等左右力戰，眾皆披靡，文帝方得乘馬。

translations.literal: Gang with Li Mu and others on either side fought fiercely, the enemy all broke and fled, and Duke Wen was only then able to remount.
translations.idiomatic: Gang with Li Mu and others fought fiercely on either side until the enemy broke and fled, and only then was Duke Wen able to remount.

sentences.zh: 大統十四年，進爵平昌郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dazong he was advanced to Duke of Pingchang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Dazong he was promoted to Duke of Pingchang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 廢帝二年，拜大將軍，兼領軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei he was appointed Grand General and concurrently made Commander of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei he was appointed Grand General and concurrently made Commander of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 及魏帝有異謀，言頗漏泄。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor harbored other designs, word leaked out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor harbored other designs, word leaked out.

sentences.zh: 周文以綱職典禁旅，使密為之備。

translations.literal: Duke Wen, because Gang's office commanded the palace guard, had him secretly prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gang's office commanded the palace guard, Duke Wen had him secretly prepare.

sentences.zh: 俄而廢帝立齊王，仍以綱為中領軍，總宿衛事。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Fei was deposed and the Prince of Qi was enthroned; Gang was still made Central Commander of the Palace Guard with overall charge of palace guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Fei was deposed and the Prince of Qi was enthroned, and Gang was still made Central Commander of the Palace Guard with overall charge of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 綱兄迥伐蜀，從周文送之於城西，見一走兔，周文命綱射之。

translations.literal: When Gang's elder brother Chijiong marched against Shu, Gang followed Duke Wen to see him off west of the city; they saw a running hare and Duke Wen ordered Gang to shoot it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gang's elder brother Chijiong marched against Shu, Gang followed Duke Wen to see him off west of the city. They saw a running hare, and Duke Wen ordered Gang to shoot it.

sentences.zh: 誓曰：「若獲此兔，必當破蜀。

translations.literal: He swore: 'If this hare is taken, Shu will surely be broken.'
translations.idiomatic: He swore, 'If this hare is taken, Shu will surely be broken.'

sentences.zh: 」俄而綱獲兔而返。

translations.literal: Soon Gang captured the hare and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gang captured the hare and returned.

sentences.zh: 周文喜曰：「事平，當賞汝佳口。

translations.literal: Duke Wen said with pleasure: 'When the matter is settled, I shall reward you with a fine mouth.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen said with pleasure, 'When the matter is settled, I shall reward you with a fine gift.'

sentences.zh: 」及克蜀，賜綱侍婢二人。

translations.literal: When Shu was taken he granted Gang two serving maids.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was taken he granted Gang two serving maids.

sentences.zh: 又嘗從周文北狩雲陽，見五鹿俱走，綱獲其三。

translations.literal: Again when he followed Duke Wen on a northern hunt at Yunyang, they saw five deer running together and Gang took three.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when he followed Duke Wen on a northern hunt at Yunyang, they saw five deer running together and Gang took three.

sentences.zh: 每從游宴，周文以珍異之物令諸功臣射而取之，綱所獲輒多。

translations.literal: Whenever he joined feasts and outings, Duke Wen would have meritorious officials shoot for rare objects; Gang always won the most.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he joined feasts and outings, Duke Wen would have the meritorious officials shoot for rare and exotic objects, and Gang always won the most.

sentences.zh: 第二子安以嫡嗣。

translations.literal: The second son An was the legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: The second son An was the legitimate heir.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位柱國。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he held rank Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he held the rank of Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 入隋，曆鴻臚卿、左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Under Sui he served in succession as Minister of Ceremonial Reception and Grand General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served in succession as Minister of Ceremonial Reception and Grand General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 安兄運。

translations.literal: An's elder brother Yun.
translations.idiomatic: An's elder brother was Yun.

sentences.zh: 運少強濟，志在立功。

translations.literal: Yun was strong and capable from youth and aspired to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yun was strong and capable and aspired to achieve merit.

sentences.zh: 魏大統十六年，以父勳封安喜縣侯。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Dazong of Wei he was enfeoffed Marquis of Anxi County for his father's merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Dazong of Wei he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anxi County for his father's merit.

sentences.zh: 周明帝立，以預定勳，進爵周城縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Zhou ascended the throne, for his merit in settling the succession he was advanced to Duke of Zhoucheng County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Zhou ascended the throne, for his merit in settling the succession he was promoted to Duke of Zhoucheng County.

sentences.zh: 歷位隴州刺史，再遷左武伯中大夫，尋加軍司馬。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Inspector of Long Province, was twice transferred to Grand Master of the Left Martial Guard, and soon given the added post of Army Vice Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as inspector of Long Province, was twice transferred to Grand Master of the Left Martial Guard, and soon given the added post of Army Vice Marshal.

sentences.zh: 運既職兼文武，甚見委任。

translations.literal: Since Yun's duties combined civil and military roles, he was greatly entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yun's duties combined civil and military roles, he was greatly entrusted.

sentences.zh: 進爵廣業郡公，轉右司衛。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Guangye Commandery and transferred to Right Director of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Duke of Guangye Commandery and transferred to Right Director of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 時宣帝在東宮，親狎諂佞，數有罪失。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xuan was in the Eastern Palace, intimate with flatterers, and often guilty of faults.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Xuan was crown prince, intimate with flatterers, and often guilty of faults.

sentences.zh: 武帝於朝臣內選忠諒鯁正者以匡弼之，於是以運為右宮正。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu selected from among the court ministers those who were loyal, honest, and upright to guide and assist him, and thus made Yun Right Director of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu selected from among the court ministers those who were loyal, honest, and upright to guide the crown prince, and thus made Yun Right Director of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，帝幸雲陽宮，又令運以本官兼司武，與長孫覽輔皇太子居守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande the emperor visited Yunyang Palace and again ordered Yun, in his existing office, to concurrently serve as Director of Martial Affairs and with Zhangsun Lan assist the crown prince in holding the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande the emperor visited Yunyang Palace and again ordered Yun, in his existing office, to concurrently serve as Director of Martial Affairs and, with Zhangsun Lan, assist the crown prince in holding the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄而衛刺王直作亂，率其党襲肅章門。

translations.literal: Soon Prince of Wei Zhi rebelled, leading his faction to raid Suzhang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Prince of Wei Zhi rebelled, leading his faction to raid the Suzhang Gate.

sentences.zh: 覽懼，走行在所。

translations.literal: Lan was afraid and fled to the emperor's temporary residence.
translations.idiomatic: Lan was afraid and fled to the emperor's temporary residence.

sentences.zh: 運時偶在門中，直兵奄至，不暇命左右，乃手自闔門。

translations.literal: Yun happened to be at the gate; Zhi's troops suddenly arrived; he had no time to order attendants and closed the gate himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yun happened to be at the gate. Zhi's troops suddenly arrived; he had no time to order his attendants and closed the gate himself.

sentences.zh: 直黨與運爭門，斫傷運指，僅而得閉。

translations.literal: Zhi's followers struggled with Yun for the gate, cut Yun's finger, and only barely got it closed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's followers struggled with Yun for the gate, cut his finger, and only barely got it closed.

sentences.zh: 直既不得入，乃縱火。

translations.literal: Zhi, unable to enter, then set fire.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to enter, Zhi then set fire.

sentences.zh: 運恐火盡，直黨得進，乃取宮中材木及床等以益火，更以膏油灌之，火轉熾。

translations.literal: Yun feared that when the fire burned out Zhi's followers would get in, so he took timber from the palace and beds to feed the fire, poured grease and oil over it, and the flames grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Yun feared that when the fire burned out Zhi's followers would get in, so he fed the flames with palace timber and beds, poured grease and oil over them, and the fire grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 久之，直不得進，乃退。

translations.literal: After a long time Zhi could not advance and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time Zhi could not advance and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 運率留守兵因其退以擊之，直大敗而走。

translations.literal: Yun led garrison troops to strike as they withdrew; Zhi was utterly defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yun led the garrison troops to strike as they withdrew, and Zhi was utterly defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 是夜微運，宮中已不守矣。

translations.literal: That night, but for Yun, the palace would no longer have been held.
translations.idiomatic: That night, but for Yun, the palace would no longer have been held.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘉之，授大將軍，賜以直田宅、妓樂、金帛、車馬、什物等不可勝數。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu praised this, appointed him Grand General, and granted Zhi's fields and mansions, musicians, gold and silk, carriages and horses, and goods beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu praised this, appointed him Grand General, and granted him Zhi's fields and mansions, musicians, gold and silk, carriages and horses, and goods beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 四年，出為同州刺史，同州、蒲津、潼關等六防諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was sent out as Inspector of Tong Province and Commander of military affairs of the six garrisons including Tong Province, Pujin, and Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was sent out as inspector of Tong Province and commander of military affairs of the six garrisons including Tong Province, Pujin, and Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 帝將伐齊，召運參議，東夏底定，頗有力焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to attack Qi he summoned Yun for deliberation; in pacifying eastern Xia Yun contributed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to attack Qi he summoned Yun for deliberation, and in pacifying eastern Xia Yun contributed greatly.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜柱國，進爵盧國公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Pillar of the State and advanced to Duke of the State of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Pillar of the State and promoted to Duke of the State of Lu.

sentences.zh: 轉司武上大夫，總宿衛軍事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Martial Affairs and given overall charge of palace guard military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Master of Martial Affairs and given overall charge of palace guard military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝崩于雲陽宮，秘未發喪，運總侍衛兵還京師。

translations.literal: When the emperor died at Yunyang Palace the death was kept secret and mourning not announced; Yun led the palace guard back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died at Yunyang Palace the death was kept secret; Yun led the palace guard back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 運弟勤，大象末，青州總管，起兵應伯迥。

translations.literal: Yun's younger brother Qin, at the end of Daxiang, was Commander of Qing Province and raised troops in response to Uncle Chijiong.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's younger brother Qin, at the end of Daxiang, was commander of Qing Province and raised troops in response to Chijiong.

sentences.zh: 勤弟敬，尚明帝女河南公主，位儀同三司。

translations.literal: Qin's younger brother Jing married Emperor Ming's daughter Princess Henan and held third-rank honorary equivalence.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's younger brother Jing married Emperor Ming's daughter Princess Henan and held third-rank honorary equivalence.

sentences.zh: 及陳將吳明徹入寇呂梁，徐州總管梁士彥頻與戰不利，乃退保州城。

translations.literal: When the Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Lüliang, Liang Shiyan, Commander of Xuzhou, repeatedly fought without success and withdrew to hold the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Lüliang, Xuzhou commander Liang Shiyan repeatedly fought without success and withdrew to hold the provincial city.

sentences.zh: 明徹遂堰清水以灌之，列船艦於城下，以圖攻取。

translations.literal: Mingche then dammed the Qing River to flood it, lined up ships below the wall, and sought to take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche then dammed the Qing River to flood the city, lined up ships below the wall, and sought to take it.

sentences.zh: 詔以軌為行軍總管，率諸軍赴救。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Gui as campaign commander to lead armies to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Gui as campaign commander to lead the armies to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 軌潛于清水入淮口，多豎大木，以鐵鎖貫車輪，橫截水流，以斷其船路，方欲密決其堰以斃之。

translations.literal: Gui secretly entered the Qing River at the Huai mouth, set up many large timbers, ran iron chains through wagon wheels to block the water crosswise and cut off their route by ship, and was about to secretly break the dam to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Gui secretly entered the Qing River at the Huai mouth, set up many large timbers, ran iron chains through wagon wheels to block the water crosswise and cut off the enemy's route by ship, and was about to secretly break the dam to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 明徹知之，乃破堰遽退，冀乘決水以得入淮。

translations.literal: Mingche learned of this, broke the dam and withdrew in haste, hoping to ride the released water into the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, Mingche broke the dam and withdrew in haste, hoping to ride the released water into the Huai.

sentences.zh: 比至清口，川流已闊，水勢亦衰，船並礙於車輪，不復得過。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Qingkou the river had widened, the force of the water had weakened, and the ships all caught on the wagon wheels and could no longer pass.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Qingkou the river had widened, the current had weakened, and the ships all caught on the wagon wheels and could no longer pass.

sentences.zh: 軌因率兵圍而蹙之。

translations.literal: Gui then led troops to surround and press them.
translations.idiomatic: Gui then led troops to surround and press them.

sentences.zh: 唯有騎將蕭摩訶以二十騎先走，得免。

translations.literal: Only cavalry general Xiao Mohe escaped first with twenty horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Only the cavalry general Xiao Mohe escaped first with twenty horsemen.

sentences.zh: 明徹及將士三萬餘人並器械輜重並就俘獲。

translations.literal: Mingche and more than thirty thousand officers and soldiers, together with weapons and baggage, were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche and more than thirty thousand officers and soldiers, together with weapons and baggage, were all captured.

sentences.zh: 陳之銳卒，於是殲焉。

translations.literal: Chen's elite troops were thus annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's elite troops were thus wiped out.

sentences.zh: 進位柱國，仍拜徐州總管。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Pillar of the State and again appointed Commander of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Pillar of the State and again appointed commander of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 軌性嚴重，善謀略，兼有呂梁之捷，威振敵境。

translations.literal: Gui was stern and grave by nature, skilled in strategy; with the victory at Lüliang his prestige shook the enemy borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was stern and grave by nature, skilled in strategy, and with the victory at Lüliang his prestige shook the enemy borderlands.

sentences.zh: 陳人甚憚之。

translations.literal: The people of Chen greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 宣帝之征吐谷渾也，武帝令軌與宇文孝伯並從，軍中進趣，皆委軌等，宣帝仰成而已。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan campaigned against Tuyuhun, Emperor Wu ordered Gui and Yuwen Xiaobo to accompany him; all military advance in the army was entrusted to Gui and the others, and Emperor Xuan had only to approve what was done.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan campaigned against Tuyuhun, Emperor Wu ordered Gui and Yuwen Xiaobo to accompany him; all military advance was entrusted to Gui and the others, and Emperor Xuan had only to approve what was done.

sentences.zh: 時宮尹鄭譯、王端並得幸于宣帝。

translations.literal: At the time palace steward Zheng Yi and Wang Duan both enjoyed Emperor Xuan's favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the palace steward Zheng Yi and Wang Duan both enjoyed Emperor Xuan's favor.

sentences.zh: 宣帝軍中頗有失德，譯等皆預焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan committed many moral lapses in the army; Yi and others all took part.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan committed many moral lapses in the army, and Yi and the others all took part.

sentences.zh: 軍還，軌等言之于武帝。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Gui and others reported this to Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Gui and the others reported this to Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 武帝大怒，乃撻宣帝，除譯等名，仍加捶楚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was greatly angered, had Emperor Xuan flogged, removed Yi and others from office, and had them beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was greatly angered, had Emperor Xuan flogged, removed Yi and the others from office, and had them beaten as well.

sentences.zh: 宣帝因此大銜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan therefore bore a deep grudge against them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan therefore bore a deep grudge against them.

sentences.zh: 軌又嘗與小內史賀若弼言及此事，且言皇太子必不克負荷。

translations.literal: Gui also once spoke of this matter with Junior Palace Secretary He Ruo Bi, and said the crown prince would surely be unable to bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Gui also once spoke of this with Junior Palace Secretary He Ruo Bi, and said the crown prince would surely be unable to bear the burden.

sentences.zh: 弼深以為然，勸軌陳之。

translations.literal: Bi deeply agreed and urged Gui to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Bi deeply agreed and urged Gui to report it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 軌後因侍坐，乃白武帝言：「皇太子多涼德，恐不了陛下家事。

translations.literal: Later, while attending the emperor, Gui reported to Emperor Wu: 'The crown prince has many moral failings, and I fear he will not be able to manage Your Majesty's household affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: Later, while attending the emperor, Gui told Emperor Wu, 'The crown prince has many moral failings, and I fear he will not be able to manage Your Majesty's household affairs.'

sentences.zh: 愚臣暗短，不足以論是非。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject is dull and limited and not fit to judge right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Your foolish subject is dull and limited and not fit to judge right and wrong.'

sentences.zh: 陛下恆以賀若弼有文武奇才，識度宏遠，而弼比再對臣，深以此事為慮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty always says He Ruo Bi has extraordinary talent in civil and military affairs and broad vision; Bi has twice spoken to me and is deeply concerned about this matter.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty always says He Ruo Bi has extraordinary talent in civil and military affairs and broad vision, and Bi has twice spoken to me and is deeply concerned about this matter.'

sentences.zh: 」武帝召弼問之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu summoned Bi and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu summoned Bi and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「皇太子養德春宮，未聞有過。

translations.literal: Bi said: 'The crown prince is cultivating virtue in the Eastern Palace, and I have heard of no faults.'
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, 'The crown prince is cultivating virtue in the Eastern Palace, and I have heard of no faults.'

sentences.zh: 未審陛下何從得聞此言？

translations.literal: I do not know from what source Your Majesty heard these words.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know from what source Your Majesty heard these words.'

sentences.zh: 」既退，軌誚弼曰：「平生言論，無所不道，今者乃爾翻覆！

translations.literal: After he withdrew, Gui reproached Bi: 'In all our talk through the years we held nothing back, yet today you turn about like this!'
translations.idiomatic: After he withdrew, Gui reproached Bi, 'In all our talk through the years we held nothing back, yet today you turn about like this!'

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「此公之過也。

translations.literal: Bi said: 'This is your fault.'
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, 'This is your fault.'

sentences.zh: 皇太子國之儲副，豈易為言，事有差跌，便至滅門之禍。

translations.literal: The crown prince is the heir of the state — how easily can one speak of him? If the matter goes awry, it leads to extermination.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is the heir of the state — how easily can one speak of him? If the matter goes awry, it leads to the calamity of extermination.'

sentences.zh: 本謂公密臧否，何得遂至昌言？

translations.literal: I thought you would keep your judgment secret — how could you speak so openly?
translations.idiomatic: I thought you would keep your judgment secret — how could you speak so openly?'

sentences.zh: 」軌默然久之，乃曰：「吾專心國家，遂不存私計。

translations.literal: Gui was silent for a long time, then said: 'I devoted myself to the state and gave no thought to private calculation.'
translations.idiomatic: Gui was silent for a long time, then said, 'I devoted myself to the state and gave no thought to private calculation.'

sentences.zh: 向者對眾，良實非宜。

translations.literal: Speaking before the assembly just now was indeed inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking before the assembly just now was indeed inappropriate.'

sentences.zh: 」其後軌因內宴上壽，又捋武帝須曰：「可愛好老公，但恨後嗣弱耳」！

translations.literal: Later, at an inner banquet when offering birthday wishes, Gui again tugged Emperor Wu's beard and said: 'What a dear old man — but how I regret that the succession is weak!'
translations.idiomatic: Later, at an inner banquet when offering birthday wishes, Gui again tugged Emperor Wu's beard and said, 'What a dear old man — but how I regret that the succession is weak!'

sentences.zh: 武帝深以為然。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu deeply agreed.

sentences.zh: 但漢王次長，又不才，此外諸子並幼，故不能用其說。

translations.literal: But the Prince of Han was next in age and also lacked talent; the other sons were all young, so he could not adopt Gui's advice.
translations.idiomatic: But the Prince of Han was next in age and also lacked talent, and the other sons were all young, so he could not adopt Gui's advice.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝即位，追鄭譯等復為近侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he recalled Zheng Yi and the others and restored them as close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he recalled Zheng Yi and the others and restored them as close attendants.

sentences.zh: 軌自知必及於禍，謂所親曰：「吾昔在先朝，實申社稷至計。

translations.literal: Gui knew disaster would surely reach him and said to those close to him: 'In the former reign I truly set forth plans vital to the altars of state.'
translations.idiomatic: Gui knew disaster would surely reach him and said to those close to him, 'In the former reign I truly set forth plans vital to the altars of state.'

sentences.zh: 今日之事，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: What will happen today can clearly be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: What will happen today can clearly be foreseen.'

sentences.zh: 此州控帶淮南，鄰接強寇，欲為身計，易同反掌。

translations.literal: This province commands Huainan and borders strong enemies; to plan for one's own safety would be as easy as turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: This province commands the Huainan region and borders strong enemies; to plan for one's own safety would be as easy as turning the hand.'

sentences.zh: 但忠義之節，不可虧違。

translations.literal: But the integrity of loyalty and righteousness cannot be compromised.
translations.idiomatic: But the integrity of loyalty and righteousness cannot be compromised.'

sentences.zh: 況荷先帝厚恩，每思以死自效，豈以獲罪於嗣主，便欲背德於先帝？

translations.literal: Moreover I have received the former emperor's deep grace and always think to repay with my life — how could I, because I have offended the succeeding ruler, wish to betray the former emperor's virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have received the former emperor's deep grace and always think to repay it with my life — how could I, because I have offended the succeeding ruler, wish to betray the former emperor's virtue?'

sentences.zh: 止可於此待死，義不為他計。

translations.literal: I can only wait here for death; in righteousness I will make no other plan.
translations.idiomatic: I can only wait here for death; in righteousness I will make no other plan.'

sentences.zh: 冀千載之後，知吾此心。」

translations.literal: I hope that a thousand years hence people will know this heart of mine.
translations.idiomatic: I hope that a thousand years hence people will know this heart of mine.'

sentences.zh: 大象元年，帝使內史杜虔信就徐州殺軌。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daxiang the emperor sent Palace Secretary Du Qianxin to Xuzhou to kill Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daxiang the emperor sent Palace Secretary Du Qianxin to Xuzhou to kill Gui.

sentences.zh: 禦正中大夫顏之儀切諫，帝不納，遂誅之。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Palace Attendants Yan Zhiyi remonstrated urgently, but the emperor did not accept it and had Gui executed.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Palace Attendants Yan Zhiyi remonstrated urgently, but the emperor refused and had Gui executed.

sentences.zh: 軌立朝忠恕，兼有大功，忽以無罪被戮，天下知與不知皆傷惜。

translations.literal: Gui served at court with loyalty and forbearance and had great merit; suddenly he was executed without crime; all under Heaven, whether they knew him or not, grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Gui served at court with loyalty and forbearance and had great merit besides; suddenly he was executed without crime, and all under Heaven, whether they knew him or not, grieved.

sentences.zh: 時京兆郡丞樂運亦以直言數諫於帝。

translations.literal: At the time Le Yun, Assistant Administrator of Jingzhao Commandery, also remonstrated with the emperor repeatedly in blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Le Yun, Assistant Administrator of Jingzhao Commandery, also remonstrated with the emperor repeatedly in blunt speech.

sentences.zh: 樂運，字承業，南陽淯陽人，晉尚書令廣之八世孫。

translations.literal: Le Yun, courtesy name Chengye, was a native of Yuyang in Nanyang and the eighth-generation descendant of Guang, Jin Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Le Yun, whose courtesy name was Chengye, came from Yuyang in Nanyang and was the eighth-generation descendant of Guang, Jin Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖文素，齊南郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wensu was Administrator of Nan Commandery under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wensu was Administrator of Nan Commandery under Qi.

sentences.zh: 父均，梁義陽郡守。

translations.literal: His father Jun was Administrator of Yiyang Commandery under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun was Administrator of Yiyang Commandery under Liang.

sentences.zh: 運少好學，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: Yun loved learning from youth and read widely in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yun loved learning and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 年十五而江陵滅，隨例遷長安。

translations.literal: At fifteen Jiangling fell and he was transferred to Chang'an according to custom.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Jiangling fell and he was transferred to Chang'an according to custom.

sentences.zh: 其親屬等多被籍沒，運積年為人傭保，皆贖免之。

translations.literal: Many of his relatives were confiscated and registered as slaves; Yun worked for years as hired laborer and redeemed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his relatives were confiscated and registered as slaves; Yun worked for years as a hired laborer and redeemed them all.

sentences.zh: 事母及寡嫂甚謹，由是以孝聞。

translations.literal: He served his mother and widowed sister-in-law with great care and thereby became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother and widowed sister-in-law with great care and thereby became known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 梁故都官郎琅邪王澄美之，次其行事為孝義傳。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng of Langya, former Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice under Liang, admired him and recorded his conduct in a biography of filial righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng of Langya, former Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice under Liang, admired him and recorded his conduct in a biography of filial righteousness.

sentences.zh: 性方直，未嘗求媚於人。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and had never sought to flatter others.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and had never sought to flatter others.

sentences.zh: 臨淄公唐瑾薦之，自柱國府記室為露門學士。

translations.literal: Duke of Linzi Tang Jin recommended him; he went from recorder in the Pillar of the State's office to Academician of the Lumengate.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Linzi Tang Jin recommended him, and he went from recorder in the Pillar of the State's office to Academician of the Lumengate.

sentences.zh: 前後犯顏屢諫武帝，多被納用。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he risked offense and remonstrated with Emperor Wu; much of what he said was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly he risked offense and remonstrated with Emperor Wu, and much of what he said was adopted.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，除萬年縣丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande he was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Wannian County.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiande he was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Wannian County.

sentences.zh: 抑挫豪右，號稱強直。

translations.literal: He checked the powerful and was known as forcefully upright.
translations.idiomatic: He checked the powerful and was known as forcefully upright.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘉之，特許通籍，事有不便於時者，令巨細奏聞。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu praised this, specially permitted him access to palace registers, and ordered that matters inconvenient to the times, great or small, be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu praised this, specially permitted him access to the palace registers, and ordered that matters inconvenient to the times, great or small, be reported.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗幸同州，召運赴行在所。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once visited Tong Province and summoned Yun to his temporary residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once visited Tong Province and summoned Yun to his temporary residence.

sentences.zh: 既至，謂曰：「卿言太子如何人？

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor said to him: 'What sort of man do you say the crown prince is?'
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the emperor said to him, 'What sort of man do you say the crown prince is?'

sentences.zh: 」運曰：「中人也。

translations.literal: Yun said: 'An average man.'
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, 'An average man.'

sentences.zh: 」時齊王憲以下並在帝側，帝顧謂憲等曰：「百官佞我，皆云太子聰明睿智，唯運雲中人，方驗運之忠直耳。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Qi Xian and those below him were all at the emperor's side. The emperor turned to Xian and the others and said: 'The officials flatter me and all say the crown prince is clever and wise; only Yun says he is an average man — this proves Yun's loyalty and bluntness.'
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Qi Xian and those below him were all at the emperor's side. The emperor turned to Xian and the others and said, 'The officials flatter me and all say the crown prince is clever and wise; only Yun says he is an average man — this proves Yun's loyalty and bluntness.'

sentences.zh: 」於是因問運中人之狀。

translations.literal: Then he asked Yun what an average man was like.
translations.idiomatic: Then he asked Yun what an average man was like.

sentences.zh: 運對曰：「班固以齊桓公為中人，管仲相之則霸，豎貂輔之則亂。

translations.literal: Yun replied: 'Ban Gu held Duke Huan of Qi to be an average man: with Guan Zhong as minister he became hegemon, with Shu Diao assisting him he fell into disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied, 'Ban Gu held Duke Huan of Qi to be an average man: with Guan Zhong as minister he became hegemon, with Shu Diao assisting him he fell into disorder.'

sentences.zh: 可與為善，亦可與為惡也。

translations.literal: He can be led to good, and he can also be led to evil.
translations.idiomatic: He can be led to good, and he can also be led to evil.'

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我知之矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I understand.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'I understand.'

sentences.zh: 」遂妙選宮官以匡弼之。

translations.literal: Then he carefully selected palace officials to guide and assist the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Then he carefully selected palace officials to guide and assist the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 乃超拜運京兆郡丞。

translations.literal: He then specially promoted Yun to Assistant Administrator of Jingzhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He then specially promoted Yun to Assistant Administrator of Jingzhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 太子聞之，意甚不悅。

translations.literal: When the crown prince heard this he was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince heard of this he was greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 及武帝崩，宣帝嗣位，葬訖，詔天下公除，帝及六宮，便議即吉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died and Emperor Xuan succeeded, after the burial an edict ordered the realm to end public mourning; the emperor and six palaces at once discussed resuming auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died and Emperor Xuan succeeded, after the burial an edict ordered the realm to end public mourning; the emperor and the six palaces at once discussed resuming auspicious dress.

sentences.zh: 運上疏曰：「三年之喪，自天子達于庶人。

translations.literal: Yun submitted a memorial saying: 'The three-year mourning applies from the Son of Heaven down to the common people.'
translations.idiomatic: Yun submitted a memorial saying, 'The three-year mourning applies from the Son of Heaven down to the common people.'

sentences.zh: 先王制禮，安可誣之。

translations.literal: The rites established by the former kings — how can they be falsely denied?
translations.idiomatic: The rites established by the former kings — how can they be falsely denied?'

sentences.zh: 禮：天子七月而葬，以候天下畢至。

translations.literal: The rites say: the Son of Heaven is buried after seven months to wait until all under Heaven have arrived.'
translations.idiomatic: The rites say the Son of Heaven is buried after seven months to wait until all under Heaven have arrived.'

sentences.zh: 今葬期既促，事訖便除，文軌之內，奔赴未盡；

translations.literal: Now the burial period has been hurried; as soon as it is over mourning ends; within the civilized realm those rushing to attend have not all arrived;
translations.idiomatic: Now the burial period has been hurried, and as soon as it is over mourning ends; within the civilized realm those rushing to attend have not all arrived;

sentences.zh: 鄰境遠聞，使猶未至。

translations.literal: in neighboring lands hearing from afar, envoys have not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: in neighboring lands hearing from afar, envoys have not yet arrived.'

sentences.zh: 若以喪服受吊，不可既吉更凶；

translations.literal: If one receives condolences in mourning dress, one cannot move from auspicious back to inauspicious;
translations.idiomatic: If one receives condolences in mourning dress, one cannot move from auspicious back to inauspicious;

sentences.zh: 如以玄冠對使，未知此出何禮？

translations.literal: if one meets envoys in the dark cap, I do not know from what rite this comes.
translations.idiomatic: if one meets envoys in the dark cap, I do not know from what rite this comes.'

sentences.zh: 進退無據，愚臣竊所未安。

translations.literal: Advancing and retreating have no basis; your foolish subject privately finds this unsettling.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing and retreating have no basis; your foolish subject privately finds this unsettling.'

sentences.zh: 」書奏，帝不納。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted the emperor did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 自是德政不修，數行赦宥。

translations.literal: From then on virtuous governance was not cultivated and amnesties were repeatedly granted.
translations.idiomatic: From then on virtuous governance was not cultivated and amnesties were repeatedly granted.

sentences.zh: 運又上疏曰：「臣謹按周官曰：'國君之過市，刑人赦。

translations.literal: Yun again submitted a memorial saying: 'Your subject respectfully notes that the Offices of Zhou says: When the ruler passes the market, criminals are pardoned.'
translations.idiomatic: Yun again submitted a memorial saying, 'Your subject respectfully notes that the Offices of Zhou says: When the ruler passes the market, criminals are pardoned.'

sentences.zh: '此謂市者交利之所，君子無故不游觀焉，則施惠以悅之也。

translations.literal: This means the market is where profit is exchanged; a gentleman does not visit it without reason, so favor is granted to please the people.
translations.idiomatic: This means the market is where profit is exchanged; a gentleman does not visit it without reason, so favor is granted to please the people.'

sentences.zh: 尚書曰：'眚災肆赦。

translations.literal: The Documents says: For inadvertent offenses and calamities, grant pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: For inadvertent offenses and calamities, grant pardon.'

sentences.zh: 」此謂過誤為害，罪雖大，當緩赦之。

translations.literal: This means harm caused by error; though the crime is great, pardon should be granted with restraint.
translations.idiomatic: This means harm caused by error; though the crime is great, pardon should be granted with restraint.'

sentences.zh: 謹尋經典，未有罪無輕重，溥天大赦之文。

translations.literal: Searching the classics carefully, there is no text of universal amnesty without distinction of guilt, light or heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Searching the classics carefully, there is no text of a universal amnesty without distinction of guilt, light or heavy.'

sentences.zh: 故管仲曰：'有赦者，奔馬之委轡；

translations.literal: Therefore Guan Zhong said: Where there is amnesty, it is like dropping the reins of a galloping horse;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Guan Zhong said: Where there is amnesty, it is like dropping the reins of a galloping horse;

sentences.zh: 不赦者，痤疽之礪石。

translations.literal: where there is no amnesty, it is like the whetstone for a carbuncle.
translations.idiomatic: where there is no amnesty, it is like the whetstone for a carbuncle.'

sentences.zh: '又曰：'惠者，人之仇讎；

translations.literal: He also said: Favor is people's enemy;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: Favor is people's enemy;

sentences.zh: 法者，人之父母。

translations.literal: law is people's parent.
translations.idiomatic: law is people's parent.'

sentences.zh: '吳漢遺言，猶雲'唯願無赦。

translations.literal: Wu Han's dying words still said: I only wish there be no amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Han's dying words still said: I only wish there be no amnesty.'

sentences.zh: '王符著論，亦云：'赦者非明世之所宜有。

translations.literal: Wang Fu in his treatise also said: Amnesty is not what a bright age ought to have.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu in his treatise also said: Amnesty is not what a bright age ought to have.'

sentences.zh: '大尊豈可數施非常之惠，以肆奸宄之惡乎。

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty repeatedly grant extraordinary favors and thereby unleash the evil of treacherous villains?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty repeatedly grant extraordinary favors and thereby unleash the evil of treacherous villains?'

sentences.zh: 」帝亦不納，而昏暴滋甚。

translations.literal: The emperor again did not accept it, and his folly and cruelty grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again refused, and his folly and cruelty grew worse.

sentences.zh: 運乃輿櫬詣朝堂，陳帝八失：

translations.literal: Yun then came to the court carrying his coffin and set forth the emperor's eight faults:
translations.idiomatic: Yun then came to the court carrying his coffin and set forth the emperor's eight faults:

sentences.zh: 一曰：內史禦正，職在弼諧，皆須參議，共理天下。

translations.literal: First: the Palace Secretary and Director of the Palace Guard have the duty of harmonizing and assisting; all must take part in deliberation and govern the realm together.
translations.idiomatic: First: the Palace Secretary and Director of the Palace Guard have the duty of harmonizing and assisting; all must take part in deliberation and govern the realm together.

sentences.zh: 大尊比來小大之事，多獨斷之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty of late decides most matters great and small alone.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty of late decides most matters great and small alone.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜至聖，尚資輔弼，況大尊未為聖主，而可專恣已心？

translations.literal: Yao and Shun, though supremely sage, still relied on assistants — how much more when Your Majesty is not yet a sage ruler can you indulge your own will alone?
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun, though supremely sage, still relied on assistants — how much more when Your Majesty is not yet a sage ruler can you indulge your own will alone?

sentences.zh: 凡諸刑罰爵賞，爰及軍國大事，請參諸宰輔，與眾共之。

translations.literal: For all punishments, rewards, enfeoffments, and military and state affairs, please consult the chief ministers and share them with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: For all punishments, rewards, enfeoffments, and military and state affairs, please consult the chief ministers and share them with the multitude.

sentences.zh: 二曰：內作色荒，古人重誡。

translations.literal: Second: dissipation within and lust without — the ancients sternly warned against this.
translations.idiomatic: Second: dissipation within and lust without — the ancients sternly warned against this.

sentences.zh: 大尊初臨四海，德惠未洽，先搜天下美女，用實後宮，又詔儀同以上女，不許輒嫁。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has just come to rule all within the seas; before virtue and grace have spread you first search the realm for beautiful women to fill the inner palace, and also decree that daughters of men with third-rank honorary equivalence and above may not marry without permission.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has just come to rule all within the seas, yet before virtue and grace have spread you first search the realm for beautiful women to fill the inner palace, and also decree that daughters of men with third-rank honorary equivalence and above may not marry without permission.

sentences.zh: 貴賤同怨，聲溢朝野。

translations.literal: Noble and common alike resented it; the outcry filled court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Noble and common alike resented it, and the outcry filled court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 請姬媵非幸禦者，放還本族。

translations.literal: Please release to their clans those concubines and attendants who have not enjoyed the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Please release to their clans those concubines and attendants who have not enjoyed the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 欲嫁之女，勿更禁之。

translations.literal: For daughters who wish to marry, do not forbid them further.
translations.idiomatic: For daughters who wish to marry, do not forbid them further.

sentences.zh: 三曰：天子未明求衣，日旰忘食，猶恐萬機不理，天下擁滯。

translations.literal: Third: the Son of Heaven seeks his robes before dawn and forgets to eat until dusk, yet still fears the myriad affairs are not managed and the realm is blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the Son of Heaven seeks his robes before dawn and forgets to eat until dusk, yet still fears that the myriad affairs are not managed and the realm is blocked and stagnant.

sentences.zh: 大尊比來一入後宮，數日不出。

translations.literal: Your Majesty of late enters the inner palace once and does not emerge for days.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty of late enters the inner palace once and does not emerge for days.

sentences.zh: 所須聞奏，多附內豎。

translations.literal: Reports that need to be heard are mostly relayed through inner eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Reports that need to be heard are mostly relayed through inner eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 傳言失實，是非可懼。

translations.literal: Messages passed along lose truth; right and wrong become fearsome.
translations.idiomatic: Messages passed along lose truth, and right and wrong become fearsome.

sentences.zh: 事由宦者，亡國之征。

translations.literal: When affairs are handled by eunuchs, it is a sign of a state's ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs are handled by eunuchs, it is a sign of a state's ruin.

sentences.zh: 請准高祖，居外聽政。

translations.literal: Please follow Gaozu's example and conduct government from outside the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Please follow Gaozu's example and conduct government from outside the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 四曰：變故易常，乃為政之大忌；

translations.literal: Fourth: changing affairs and altering constants is a great taboo in governance;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: changing affairs and altering constants is a great taboo in governance;

sentences.zh: 淫刑酷罰，非致安之弘規。

translations.literal: excessive punishments and cruel penalties are not the broad policy for securing peace.
translations.idiomatic: excessive punishments and cruel penalties are not the broad policy for securing peace.

sentences.zh: 若罰無定刑，則天下皆懼；

translations.literal: If punishments have no fixed standards, then all under Heaven will fear;
translations.idiomatic: If punishments have no fixed standards, then all under Heaven will fear;

sentences.zh: 政無常法，則人無適從。

translations.literal: if government has no constant law, then people have nothing to follow.
translations.idiomatic: if government has no constant law, then people have nothing to follow.

sentences.zh: 豈有削嚴刑之詔未及半祀，便即遣改，更嚴前制？

translations.literal: How can there be an edict reducing severe punishments not yet half a year old that is at once changed and made stricter than before?
translations.idiomatic: How can an edict reducing severe punishments, not yet half a year old, be changed at once and made stricter than before?

sentences.zh: 政令不定，乃至於此！

translations.literal: Government orders are unsettled to this degree!
translations.idiomatic: Government orders are unsettled to this degree!

sentences.zh: 今宿衛之官，有一夜不直者，罪至削除；

translations.literal: Now among the palace guard, one night off duty leads to punishment as far as removal from office;
translations.idiomatic: Now among the palace guard, one night off duty leads to punishment as far as removal from office;

sentences.zh: 因而逃亡者，遂便籍沒。

translations.literal: those who flee are at once confiscated and registered as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: those who flee are at once confiscated and registered as slaves.

sentences.zh: 此則大逆之罪，與杖十同科。

translations.literal: Thus the crime of great treason is placed in the same category as ten strokes of the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the crime of great treason is placed in the same category as ten strokes of the rod.

sentences.zh: 雖為法愈嚴，恐人情愈散。

translations.literal: Though the law grows ever stricter, I fear hearts grow ever more scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Though the law grows ever stricter, I fear hearts grow ever more scattered.

sentences.zh: 一人心散，尚或不可止，若天下皆散，將如之何？

translations.literal: If one person's heart scatters, it may still be unstoppable; if all under Heaven scatter, what then?
translations.idiomatic: If one person's heart scatters, it may still be unstoppable; if all under Heaven scatter, what then?

sentences.zh: 請遵輕典，並依大律，則億兆之人，手足有所措矣。

translations.literal: Please follow the lighter code and rely on the great statutes; then the hundred million people will know where to set hand and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Please follow the lighter code and rely on the great statutes, and then the hundred million people will know where to set hand and foot.

sentences.zh: 五曰：高祖ＩＸ雕為樸，本欲傳之萬世。

translations.literal: Fifth: Gaozu cut ornamentation to keep things plain, intending this to be handed down for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: Gaozu cut ornamentation to keep things plain, intending this to be handed down for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 大尊朝夕趨庭，親承聖旨。

translations.literal: Your Majesty morning and evening attended in the court and personally received the sage's instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty morning and evening attended in the court and personally received the sage's instructions.

sentences.zh: 豈有崩未逾年，而遽窮奢麗，成父之志，義豈然乎？

translations.literal: How can it be, before a year has passed since his death, that you suddenly exhaust yourself in luxury — is this fulfilling your father's intent?
translations.idiomatic: How can it be, before a year has passed since his death, that you suddenly exhaust yourself in luxury — is this fulfilling your father's intent?

sentences.zh: 請興造之制，務從卑儉，雕文刻鏤，一切勿營。

translations.literal: Please make construction regulations insist on humility and frugality; undertake no carved or inlaid ornamentation at all.
translations.idiomatic: Please make construction regulations insist on humility and frugality, and undertake no carved or inlaid ornamentation at all.

sentences.zh: 六曰：都下之人，徭賦稍重。

translations.literal: Sixth: for the people of the capital, corvée and taxes are somewhat heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: for the people of the capital, corvée and taxes are somewhat heavy.

sentences.zh: 必是軍國之要，不敢憚勞。

translations.literal: This must be for the needs of army and state; they dare not shrink from labor.
translations.idiomatic: This must be for the needs of army and state, and they dare not shrink from labor.

sentences.zh: 豈容朝夕徵求，唯供魚龍爛漫；

translations.literal: How can daily levies be tolerated merely to supply fish, dragons, and lavish entertainments;
translations.idiomatic: How can daily levies be tolerated merely to supply fish, dragons, and lavish entertainments;

sentences.zh: 士庶從役，只為俳優角抵？

translations.literal: gentry and commoners serve corvée only for actors and wrestlers?
translations.idiomatic: gentry and commoners serve corvée only for actors and wrestlers?

sentences.zh: 紛紛不已，財力俱竭，業業相顧，無復聊生。

translations.literal: The demands continue without end; wealth and strength are both exhausted; people look at one another in dread; there is no longer any ease in life.
translations.idiomatic: The demands continue without end, wealth and strength are both exhausted, people look at one another in dread, and there is no longer any ease in life.

sentences.zh: 凡無益之事，請並停罷。

translations.literal: For all useless activities, please stop them together.
translations.idiomatic: For all useless activities, please stop them together.

sentences.zh: 七曰：近見有詔，上書字誤者即科其罪。

translations.literal: Seventh: recently there was an edict that those who make errors in characters in memorials are immediately punished.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: recently there was an edict that those who make errors in characters in memorials are immediately punished.

sentences.zh: 假有忠讜之人，欲陳時事，尺有所短，文字非工，不密失身，義無假手，脫有舛謬，便迫嚴科。

translations.literal: Suppose there is a loyal and outspoken man who wishes to report on current affairs: the foot has its short measure, his writing is not polished, he cannot conceal himself without risk, and in righteousness he has no one to write for him — if there is any error, he immediately faces severe punishment.
