translations.idiomatic: Suppose there is a loyal and outspoken man who wishes to report on current affairs: the foot has its short measure, his writing is not polished, he cannot conceal himself without risk, and in righteousness he has no one to write for him — if there is any error, he immediately faces severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 嬰徑尺之鱗，其事非易；

translations.literal: For Yan Ying to touch a foot-long scale was no easy matter;
translations.idiomatic: For Yan Ying to touch a foot-long scale was no easy matter;

sentences.zh: 下不諱之詔，猶懼未來。

translations.literal: even an edict against taboo words still feared what might come.
translations.idiomatic: even an edict against taboo words still feared what might come.

sentences.zh: 更加刑戮，能無鉗口？

translations.literal: Add execution on top of this — how can mouths not be silenced?
translations.idiomatic: Add execution on top of this — how can mouths not be silenced?

sentences.zh: 大尊縱不能采誹謗之言，無宜杜獻替之路。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, even if you cannot adopt words of criticism, you should not block the path of remonstrance and correction.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, even if you cannot adopt words of criticism, you should not block the path of remonstrance and correction.

sentences.zh: 請停此詔，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Please stop this edict, and all under Heaven will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Please stop this edict, and all under Heaven will be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 八曰：或桑谷生朝，殷王因之獲福，今玄象垂戒，此亦興周之祥。

translations.literal: Eighth: once mulberry and grain grew in the court hall and the king of Yin thereby gained blessing; now celestial signs send warning — this too may be an omen of Zhou's rise.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: once mulberry and grain grew in the court hall and the king of Yin thereby gained blessing; now celestial signs send warning — this too may be an omen of Zhou's rise.

sentences.zh: 大尊雖滅膳撤縣，未盡銷譴之理。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, though you reduce meals and withdraw music, has not fully dispelled the logic of reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, though you reduce meals and withdraw music, has not fully dispelled the logic of reproach.

sentences.zh: 誠願諮諏善道，修布德政，解兆庶之慍，引萬方之罪。

translations.literal: I truly wish you would consult the good Way, cultivate and spread virtuous governance, release the resentment of the masses, and draw the guilt of all regions upon yourself.
translations.idiomatic: I truly wish you would consult the good Way, cultivate and spread virtuous governance, release the resentment of the masses, and draw the guilt of all regions upon yourself.

sentences.zh: 則天變可除，鼎業方固。

translations.literal: Then celestial changes can be removed and the imperial enterprise will be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Then celestial changes can be removed and the imperial enterprise will be secure.

sentences.zh: 大尊若不革茲八事，臣見周廟不血食矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not reform these eight matters, I see that the Zhou ancestral temple will receive no blood offerings.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not reform these eight matters, I see that the Zhou ancestral temple will receive no blood offerings.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，將戮之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered and was about to execute him.

sentences.zh: 內史元嚴諫，因而獲免。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Yuan Yan remonstrated, and Yun was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Yuan Yan remonstrated, and Yun was thereby spared.

sentences.zh: 翌日，帝頗感悟，召運謂之曰：「朕昨夜思卿所奏，實是忠臣。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor was somewhat moved, summoned Yun, and said: 'Last night I reflected on what you submitted — you are truly a loyal subject.'
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor was somewhat moved, summoned Yun, and said, 'Last night I reflected on what you submitted — you are truly a loyal subject.'

sentences.zh: 先皇聖明，卿數有規諫；

translations.literal: The former emperor was sage and bright, and you remonstrated with him many times;
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor was sage and bright, and you remonstrated with him many times;

sentences.zh: 朕既昏暗，卿復能如此！

translations.literal: I am dull and dark, yet you were still able to do this!
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and dark, yet you were still able to do this!'

sentences.zh: 」乃賜禦食以賞之。

translations.literal: Then he granted him imperial food as a reward.
translations.idiomatic: Then he granted him imperial food as a reward.

sentences.zh: 朝之公卿，初見帝甚怒，莫不為運寒心。

translations.literal: The nobles at court, when they first saw the emperor's great anger, all feared for Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The nobles at court, when they first saw the emperor's great anger, all feared for Yun.

sentences.zh: 後見獲賞，又皆相賀，以為倖免獸口。

translations.literal: Later when they saw he was rewarded, they all congratulated one another, thinking he had escaped the beast's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when they saw he was rewarded, they all congratulated one another, thinking he had escaped the beast's mouth.

sentences.zh: 內史鄭譯常以私事請托，運不之許，因此銜之。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Zheng Yi often asked favors for private matters, and Yun did not grant them, so Yi bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Zheng Yi often asked favors for private matters, and Yun refused, so Yi bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝為丞相，譯為長史，遂左遷運為廣州滍陽令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui became chancellor and Yi became chief administrator, Yun was demoted to Magistrate of Ziyang in Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui became chancellor and Yi became chief administrator, Yun was demoted to Magistrate of Ziyang in Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 開皇五年，轉毛州高唐令。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaihuang he was transferred to Magistrate of Gaotang in Mao Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaihuang he was transferred to Magistrate of Gaotang in Mao Province.

sentences.zh: 頻曆二縣，並有聲績。

translations.literal: Serving in succession in two counties, he had reputation and achievement in both.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in succession in two counties, he earned reputation and achievement in both.

sentences.zh: 運常願處一諫官，從容諷議，而性訐直，為人所排抵，遂不被任用。

translations.literal: Yun always wished to hold a remonstrating office and offer measured criticism, but by nature he was blunt and upright, was blocked by others, and was therefore not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Yun always wished to hold a remonstrating office and offer measured criticism, but by nature he was blunt and upright, was blocked by others, and was therefore not employed.

sentences.zh: 乃發憤錄夏、殷以來諫爭事，集而部之，凡六百三十九條，合四十一卷，名曰諫苑。

translations.literal: Then in indignation he recorded remonstrances from Xia and Yin onward, collected and arranged them — six hundred thirty-nine entries in all, forty-one volumes, entitled Garden of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Then in indignation he recorded remonstrances from Xia and Yin onward, collected and arranged them — six hundred thirty-nine entries in all, forty-one volumes, entitled Garden of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 奏上之。

translations.literal: He submitted it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝覽而嘉焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui read it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui read it and praised it.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王羆剛峭有餘，弘雅未之聞也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Wang Pi had more than enough blunt severity; magnanimity and refinement were not heard of in him.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Wang Pi had more than enough blunt severity; magnanimity and refinement were not heard of in him.

sentences.zh: 情安儉率，志在公平。

translations.literal: He was content with frugality and plainness and set his heart on fairness.
translations.idiomatic: He was content with frugality and plainness and set his heart on fairness.

sentences.zh: 既而奮節危城，抗辭勍敵，梁人為之退舍，高氏不敢加兵。

translations.literal: Then he upheld integrity in a perilous city and answered a fierce enemy with bold words; the people of Liang withdrew before him, and the Gao clan dared not send troops.
translations.idiomatic: Then he upheld integrity in a perilous city and answered a fierce enemy with bold words; the Liang withdrew before him, and the Gao clan dared not send troops.

sentences.zh: 以此見稱，信非虛矣。

translations.literal: To be praised for this was truly no empty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: To be praised for this was truly no empty reputation.

sentences.zh: 至述不隕門風，亦足稱也。

translations.literal: As for Shu, he did not disgrace the family tradition — that too is worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: As for Shu, he did not disgrace the family tradition — that too is worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 王思政驅馳有事之秋，慷慨功名之際。

translations.literal: Wang Sizheng rushed about in a season of urgent affairs and was impassioned in the pursuit of merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng rushed about in a season of urgent affairs and was impassioned in the pursuit of merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 及乎策名霸府，作鎮潁川，設縈帶之險，修守禦之術，以一城之眾，抗傾國之師，率疲駘之兵，當勁勇之卒，猶能亟摧大敵，屢建奇功。

translations.literal: When he achieved name in the hegemon's office and governed Yingchuan, he set up the danger of encircling terrain and perfected methods of defense; with the people of one city he resisted a nation's army, leading weary troops against fierce soldiers, yet could quickly crush great enemies and repeatedly achieve strange merit.
translations.idiomatic: When he achieved name in the hegemon's office and governed Yingchuan, he set up the danger of encircling terrain and perfected methods of defense; with the people of one city he resisted a nation's army, leading weary troops against fierce soldiers, yet could quickly crush great enemies and repeatedly achieve strange merit.

sentences.zh: 忠節冠於本朝，義聲動於鄰聽。

translations.literal: Loyal integrity crowned the court, and the voice of righteousness moved neighboring listeners.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal integrity crowned the court, and the voice of righteousness moved neighboring listeners.

sentences.zh: 運窮事蹙，城陷身囚，壯志高風亦足奮於百世矣。

translations.literal: When fortune ran out and affairs pressed tight, the city fell and he was taken prisoner, yet his great resolve and lofty spirit are enough to inspire for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: When fortune ran out and affairs pressed tight, the city fell and he was taken prisoner, yet his great resolve and lofty spirit are enough to inspire for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥地則舅甥，職惟台袞，沐恩累葉，荷眷一時，居形勝之地，受籓維之托，顛而不扶，憂責斯在？

translations.literal: Wei Chijiong was related as uncle and nephew by territory, his office was among the highest ministers, he received grace through successive generations and favor in his time, occupied a strategically vital place, and was entrusted with the defense of the realm — when it tottered and he did not support it, was not the burden of concern his?
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chijiong was related as uncle and nephew by territory, his office was among the highest ministers, he received grace through successive generations and favor in his time, occupied a strategically vital place, and was entrusted with the defense of the realm — when it tottered and he did not support it, was not the burden of concern his?

sentences.zh: 及主威雲謝，鼎業將遷，九服移心，三靈改卜，遂能志存赴蹈，投袂稱兵。

translations.literal: When the ruler's authority faded like clouds and the imperial enterprise was about to shift, the nine domains changed heart and the three spirits altered their divination, he was able to keep his will set on rushing forward, throw up his sleeves, and raise arms.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler's authority faded like clouds and the imperial enterprise was about to shift, the nine domains changed heart and the three spirits altered their divination, he was able to keep his will set on rushing forward, throw up his sleeves, and raise arms.

sentences.zh: 忠君之勤未宣，違天之禍便及。

translations.literal: His loyalty to the ruler was not yet proclaimed, but the calamity of defying Heaven soon reached him.
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty to the ruler was not yet proclaimed, but the calamity of defying Heaven soon reached him.

sentences.zh: 校其心，翟義、葛誕之儔歟。

translations.literal: Compare his heart — is he not of the company of Zhai Yi and Ge Dan?
translations.idiomatic: Compare his heart — is he not of the company of Zhai Yi and Ge Dan?

sentences.zh: 綱、運積宣王室，勤勞出內。

translations.literal: Gang and Yun accumulated service to the royal house, their labor extending from within.
translations.idiomatic: Gang and Yun accumulated service to the royal house, their labor extending from within.

sentences.zh: 觀其自致榮寵，豈唯恩澤而已乎？

translations.literal: Observing how they attained glory and favor themselves, was it only through grace and favor?
translations.idiomatic: Observing how they attained glory and favor themselves, was it only through grace and favor?

sentences.zh: 夫士之成名，其途不一，蓋有不待爵祿而貴，不因學藝而重者何？

translations.literal: For a gentleman to achieve a name, the paths are not one; are there not those who are honored without waiting for rank and salary, and esteemed without relying on learning and skill?
translations.idiomatic: For a gentleman to achieve a name, the paths are not one; are there not those who are honored without waiting for rank and salary, and esteemed without relying on learning and skill?

sentences.zh: 亦云忠孝而已。

translations.literal: It is also said to be loyalty and filial piety alone.
translations.idiomatic: It is also said to be loyalty and filial piety alone.

sentences.zh: 若乃竭力以奉其親者，人子之行也；

translations.literal: To exert one's strength in serving one's parents is the conduct of a son;
translations.idiomatic: To exert one's strength in serving one's parents is the conduct of a son;

sentences.zh: 致身以事其君者，人臣之節也。

translations.literal: to give one's person in serving one's ruler is the integrity of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: to give one's person in serving one's ruler is the integrity of a subject.

sentences.zh: 斯固彌綸三極，囊括百代。

translations.literal: These indeed extend through the three poles and encompass a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: These indeed extend through the three poles and encompass a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 當宣帝之在東朝，凶德方兆，王軌志惟無諱，極議於骨肉之間，竟遇淫刑，以至夷滅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was in the Eastern Palace, evil conduct was just emerging; Wang Gui's will was only to speak without concealment, and he argued to the limit among close kin, yet in the end met excessive punishment and was exterminated to the last.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was crown prince, evil conduct was just emerging; Wang Gui's will was only to speak without concealment, and he argued to the limit among close kin, yet in the end met excessive punishment and was exterminated to the last.

sentences.zh: 若斯人者，人或以為其不忠，則天下莫之信也。

translations.literal: For such a man, if some think him disloyal, none under Heaven will believe it.
translations.idiomatic: For such a man, if some think him disloyal, none under Heaven will believe it.

sentences.zh: 觀樂運之所以行已之節，其有古之遺直之風乎。

translations.literal: Observing the integrity with which Le Yun conducted himself, does he not have the wind of the blunt integrity of antiquity?
translations.idiomatic: Observing the integrity with which Le Yun conducted himself, does he not have the wind of the blunt integrity of antiquity?
